stories.title: Panchayat Elections in UP will be held between April-July:Minister OP Rajbhar says, 'Ballot papers have reached districts, voter list will come on February 28'
stories.summary: UP Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar on Tuesday made a major statement on the state’s panchayat elections, saying the government has completed all preparations and the polls will be held on time. Rajbhar, who is a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, made the remarks while speaking in Varanasi. He ruled out speculation that the panchayat elections would be held along with the 2027 Assembly elections. He said the state government is fully prepared and there is no plan to delay the panchayat polls. He said- Panchayat elections will be held before assembly elections. Ballot papers have been printed and reached all districts for this. District Election Officers have started their homework. Final publication of voter list on February 28 Rajbhar said - The final publication of the voter list will be on February 28, 2026. Prospective candidates have been advised to get their supporters' names added before the final list comes out. Panchayat elections will not be conducted on EVMs but through ballot papers. Preparations ongoing in districts UP Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has clarified that the three-tier elections for Pradhan, District Panchayat Member and Kshetra Panchayat Member will be held on time. The government is fully prepared for this. Preparations are underway in every district. Elections will be held between April and July OP Rajbhar said - Panchayat elections will be held before the assembly elections. However, he avoided announcing exact dates yet. Said - The entire process of panchayat elections will be completed between April to July 2026. In the first phase, votes will be cast for Gram Pradhan, BDC (Kshetra Panchayat member) and District Panchayat members. This will be followed by indirect elections for Block Chief and District Panchayat President. Districts are ready for this and ballot papers have been delivered to the districts. Their notification will be done soon. Response given to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's statement OP Rajbhar said - The country will run according to the Constitution. Not by any Shankaracharya's statement. The constitution will not change by anyone's statement. The government is running according to that constitution. New laws won't be made just because someone says so. Neither Government nor Organization Want Timely Elections According to BJP sources, both the party and government are not in favor of holding timely elections. There are several political risks in panchayat elections before the assembly elections. Firstly, political animosity between party workers in villages will increase. Secondly, party workers who are unhappy with candidate selection may take tickets from other parties and weaken the party. If the party's performance in the district panchayat member and area panchayat member elections is not good, it will directly affect the assembly elections. Even in 2021, the experience of the first phase of panchayat elections was not good for the Yogi government and BJP. A lot of effort had to be made to control that damage. According to sources, in the recent core group meeting of the party and government, there was also discussion on this issue that the panchayat elections should be postponed until after the assembly elections. What will happen if panchayat elections are postponed? The term of village heads, area panchayat members and district panchayat members in the state will end in the first week of May. Meanwhile, the five-year term of block chiefs and district panchayat presidents will be completed in the first week of July. In such a situation, if elections are not held on time, a competent officer will be appointed as receiver (administrator) by the government in place of village heads, block chiefs and district panchayat presidents.

stories.title: SP MPs protest in Parliament over Manikarnika Ghat controversy:Protesters hold Ahilyabai’s picture, say Kashi’s identity is being erased
stories.summary: The issue of Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi reached Parliament on Tuesday during the Budget Session, with opposition parties staging strong protests outside the Parliament building. Several Samajwadi Party (SP) MPs, including Ram Gopal Yadav and Dharmendra Yadav, held demonstrations while carrying pictures of Ahilyabai Holkar. The MPs raised slogans against the central government and accused it of undermining Kashi’s cultural and historical identity. Chanting slogans such as “India will not tolerate the insult of Rajmata”, the protesting MPs launched a sharp attack on the government, alleging that the traditions and heritage of Kashi were being systematically damaged. SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav said the demolition of Ahilyabai Holkar’s statue amounted to an assault on Kashi’s cultural legacy. Calling it interference with history and faith, he alleged that the demolition at Manikarnika Ghat was carried out without proper planning. He said Banaras has a unique and ancient culture, reflected in its narrow lanes, temples and long-standing traditions, all of which are now under threat. Ram Gopal Yadav also pointed out that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the MP from Varanasi, yet the city’s cultural heritage continues to suffer. He said the people of Banaras have always opposed changes that harm their culture, and warned that efforts are being made to erase the city’s identity. stories.title: Yogi Adityanath defends police encounters:CM says lawbreakers are dealt in language they understand
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday strongly defended his government’s policy of zero tolerance towards crime, saying the state was once gripped by violence and lawlessness. “Between 2012 and 2017, there were more than 900 riots. There was hardly any city that did not witness repeated curfews. There was no businessman who was not forced to pay extortion money. Crime dominated every sphere of life. I was given responsibility at such a time, and we decided on zero tolerance,” the Chief Minister said. Yogi Adityanath asserted that the law applies equally to everyone. “If someone from our own side commits a crime, the same law will apply to them as it does to mafias and criminals,” he said. Addressing criticism over police encounters, the Chief Minister questioned the expectations placed on law enforcement. “Many people ask why the police fire shots. If the police do not fire, then what should they do? Both things cannot work together,” he remarked. If criminals are free to fire bullets: Yogi defends police He further said that if criminals have the freedom to use weapons, the police must also be empowered to respond. “If criminals are free to fire bullets, then pistols have also been given to the police so they can confront criminals head-on. The police have been specially trained to deal with criminals in the language they understand,” Yogi said. These statements were made during the inauguration of UP Pharma Conclave 1.0 in Lucknow. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak was also present at the event. On the occasion, the state government signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with 11 companies, aimed at joint research in medical devices and the development of new medicines. Key Points from Yogi's Address 1. Before 2017, there were riots and companies were migrating Yogi said - Before 2017, there were riots. Kidnappings were common. There wasn't a single doctor, trader, or businessman who hadn't paid extortion money. Youth were migrating. Companies were relocating. When there's no security, how can businesses stay? Even the existing enterprises started leaving. This was everyone's pain. It's very painful to leave the land where you spent your childhood. This is the pain of every person who has seen that era. 2. Choose pick won't work, action against our own people too Yogi said - In 2017, PM Modi gave me the responsibility. When we looked at it, we decided on zero tolerance. Choose and pick won't work, meaning if our own person does wrong, action will be taken against them. There will be no discrimination between our own and others. When we started taking action, we tried to stay within the bounds of law, but many times if someone was not afraid of the law, then bringing such a person within the law's framework and making them understand the language of law becomes an immediate necessity. 3. When explained, big tasks became easier Yogi said - When criminals, mafias and anarchic elements were made to understand, big tasks started becoming easier. There were no incidents of peace disruption, no cases of anarchy, no instances of hooliganism. There are no riots or conflicts. Today there is no such situation anywhere. UP is establishing excellent standards for investment. 4. No liberty to play with the law Yogi said - No one has the liberty to play with the law. If anyone challenges the law, the law brings them within its boundaries and makes them understand in its own way. There was a time when people in UP felt distrust and insecurity because of anarchy. Today that has become a thing of the past. 5. Have to conduct rehearsals to deal with pre-2017 situations Yogi said - I have to teach my people how to deal with pre-2017 situations. Sometimes we have to conduct rehearsals about what to do if a riot breaks out, because in 9 years people have forgotten what a riot is like. Since they can't riot during my tenure, I have to stand up myself and say now demonstrate in front of me. 6. India will not bow to anyone Yogi said, “We are grateful to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump for rolling back and reducing tariffs on India and recognising India as a trusted partner. India stood firm on its policies, and the result is Satyameva Jayate (truth always prevails). This has happened before and will continue to happen in the future.” 7. 65,000 acres of land freed within 24 hours Yogi said, “When we came to power in 2017, it was impossible to find land anywhere in Uttar Pradesh. No land was available because land mafias had occupied it. We formed a land-mafia task force and I announced a 24-hour deadline. I said that any land mafia occupying government land in Uttar Pradesh must vacate it immediately. “If action was required after 24 hours, the law would take its own course. Not only would they be forced to vacate the land, but the illegal earnings made from it would also be recovered with interest. “You would be surprised to know that 65,000 acres of land were vacated. This became our land bank, which we now utilise according to our development plans.”

stories.title: Officer arrested for taking leave without informing in Meerut:Kept in police custody for three hours, claims wife unwell
stories.summary: In a strict administrative action, a Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) in Meerut had a Block Education Officer (BEO) arrested for proceeding on leave without prior approval, allegedly disrupting crucial voter list revision work. The arrested officer, Shyam Mohan Asthana, was taken into police custody for nearly three hours and subjected to a medical examination before being released. The incident occurred after the SDM filed a police complaint citing dereliction of duty. Absence affected Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter list According to SDM Udit Narayan Sengar, Asthana was posted as Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter list. He was responsible for conducting timely hearings and submitting reports related to SIR notices. However, the officer allegedly failed to perform his assigned duties and did not inform senior officials before leaving, leading to a complete halt of SIR-related work. Officer missing since Saturday without approved leave Officials said Asthana had been absent since Saturday without any sanctioned leave. Despite being assigned the critical responsibility of hearing SIR-related cases at the tehsil auditorium, he neither attended the hearings nor communicated his absence. As a result, administrative work was disrupted and voters faced inconvenience. SDM files police complaint Terming the matter as gross negligence and indiscipline in government duty, SDM Sengar submitted a written complaint to the police. Acting on the complaint, the police detained the officer and brought him to the police station. During the inquiry, it emerged that Asthana had applied for leave, but it was not approved. Despite this, he left the station and could not be reached on phone calls. Officials said efforts were made to call him back, but he returned only later. Officer’s clarification: Wife was unwell Defending himself, Asthana stated that both he and his wife were unwell, which forced him to travel to Lucknow. He maintained that he had applied for leave, though it was not sanctioned. Naib Tehsildar assigned SIR responsibility To ensure smooth functioning of voter list revision work, Naib Tehsildar Bhupendra Kumar has been assigned the responsibility of conducting SIR hearings in place of the Block Education Officer. “Negligence will not be tolerated,” says SDM SDM Udit Narayan Sengar said that negligence in government work will not be tolerated at any level. He added that a formal letter has also been sent to the Basic Education Officer (BEO) for further departmental inquiry and action. Officials view the move as a strong signal to enforce discipline and accountability in government functioning.

stories.title: Former MP stopped at Mika Singh concert in Aligarh:Supporters say ‘He is a leader’; PAC still refuses entry, calls senior officer
stories.summary: A tense situation erupted at a live concert by Bollywood singer Mika Singh in Aligarh on Sunday evening after security personnel stopped a former Member of Parliament at the entry gate, leading to a prolonged argument and brief scuffle. Uttar Pradesh Provincial Armed Constabulary (UP-PAC) jawans deployed at the venue refused entry to former MP Raju Bhaiya and his supporters, citing heavy crowding. Despite repeated attempts by his supporters to explain that he was a former MP and political leader, security personnel did not allow him inside. Pictures first- Pushing and shoving as argument drags on for half an hour The argument at the gate continued for nearly 30 minutes and escalated into pushing and shoving. As the situation threatened to spiral out of control, senior police officers were called to the spot. Following their intervention, permission was granted and the former MP was eventually allowed to enter the venue. A video of the incident has since surfaced and is circulating on social media. Mika Singh concert draws massive crowd at Aligarh Festival The concert was held on February 2 at the Kohinoor Stage at the Numaish ground as part of the Aligarh Festival. Seating arrangements were made for around 2,500 people. The programme was scheduled to begin at 7 pm, but a large crowd began gathering well before that. By 8 pm, the pandal was completely packed, with thousands more attempting to enter the venue. Police halt entry citing overcrowding, spectators protest Seeing the swelling crowd at the main gate, police temporarily stopped entry to prevent overcrowding. This triggered anger among spectators, many of whom raised slogans and insisted on being allowed inside. Heated exchanges were reported between the crowd and the police during this period. Amid this chaos, the former MP arrived with his supporters from Etah. Even after being identified by party workers, PAC jawans refused entry due to safety concerns. The former MP then sought to speak with senior officers, after which clearance was granted. Police officials later said the restrictions were imposed strictly in the interest of public safety, as the venue had already reached full capacity.

stories.title: ‘Consensual physical relationship is not a crime’:Allahabad High Court quashes FIR; case linked to false marriage promise
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ruled that consensual physical relations cannot later be treated as fraud. The court said that if two adults enter a relationship with consent, it does not become a crime just because the relationship later breaks down. While hearing the case, the court explained that disappointment or emotional hurt after a failed relationship cannot be seen as cheating or fraud. Such situations, the court said, are part of personal relationships and not criminal acts. The High Court clarified that Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita applies only when a relationship is formed through clear deceit, such as a false promise of marriage made with dishonest intent. The law does not cover cases where a consensual relationship ends badly. Section 69 provides for punishment of up to 10 years in jail if a person is found guilty of forming a relationship through fraud or deception. A division bench of Justice Siddharth Verma and Justice Abdul Shahid made these remarks while ordering that the FIR in the case be quashed. Now let's know the full case in detail The case is from Noida. On December 12, 2024, a young woman filed an FIR at Sector-63 police station against a young man, accusing him of threatening, assaulting, and making relations by falsely promising marriage (Section-69). The accused young man filed a petition in the High Court to quash the FIR. The young man's lawyer informed the court during the hearing that the young woman and the accused young man had studied LLM together in Jodhpur. During this time, they became friends. Both agreed to get married. They got engaged in June 2023. After the engagement, the wedding date was set for November 12, 2024. After the wedding date was fixed, both families started wedding preparations. The petitioner presented evidence in court of hotel booking, wedding card printing, and photographer booking. Court said - cannot be considered fraud After hearing both sides, the court found that the petitioner had started wedding preparations. Later, for some reason, the relationship broke down. Differences arose between them. The court found that the promise of marriage made was genuine. It cannot be considered fraud retrospectively. FIR registered under Section 69 cancelled An offense under Section-69 is constituted only when the man had no intention of marrying from the beginning and had made a false promise only for the relationship. The court cancelled the FIR registered under Section 69. However, it has ordered an investigation into the FIR registered for threatening, assaulting, and other charges.

stories.title: Brainwashing, forced Namaz alleged at Mathura school:Headmaster accused of religious indoctrination, discouraging national anthem; parents, students deny claims
stories.summary: Two serious allegations were made against the headmaster of a primary school in Mathura. First- He brainwashes young children studying in the school. He describes Islam as better and Hinduism as bad. Second- He forcibly makes them offer Namaz (Islamic prayer) in school and does not conduct the national anthem. Within 24 hours, Headmaster Jan Mohammad was suspended by the Basic Education Officer (BSA). After this, Jan Mohammad's health deteriorated. He took leave and went to his home in Agra. Was an Islamic environment really being created in the school? Are the complainants' parents? To find out all this, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached the Nauhjheel area. There was a crowd of parents and children inside and outside the school. During the conversation, it came to light that a total of 235 children study here. Of these, 89 are Muslim, and the rest are Hindu children. There are 8 people deployed in the school staff, 7 of whom are Hindu. This means only the headmaster is non-Hindu. We spoke to everyone. A new story emerged. This whole matter revolves around the allegations of a local BJP leader. It also came to light that action was taken after the complaint, but the investigation has not yet begun. The teachers were surprised by allegations such as forced prayer (Namaz) and not having the national anthem. Disputes arose here - the land adjacent to the school campus was coming within the boundary wall's purview. This was being opposed by a particular group. Those who complained are said to belong to the same group. Read the full report... Know where this matter started BJP leader said - children sing national anthem, headmaster scolds... BJP's Bajna Mandal President Durgesh Pradhan sent a letter to BSA Ratan Kirti on January 30. He alleged that in the school, Headmaster Jan Mohammad entices children and inspires them towards Islam. He brainwashes children and makes them offer Namaz. He insults Hindu deities. He also makes objectionable comments about Hinduism. In the school campus, in the presence of the headmaster, people from Tablighi Jamaat are called from outside. These people pressure children to adopt Islam. Children are also told that Islam is the best religion in the world. The national anthem is not performed in the school. If children try to sing the national anthem, they are scolded. The headmaster himself never performs the national anthem. When Durgesh Pradhan was asked, "How did you come to know all these facts? Did you go there yourself to see?" He said that people from the village itself came to him with complaints. After this, I sent a letter to the Block Education Officer. The Block Education Officer sent the letter to the BSA. After that, on January 31, Headmaster Jan Mohammad was suspended. This school was affiliated with Primary School Nagla Humayun, Mant. The BSA has formed a team of BEO Chhata and BEO Mant for a detailed investigation. This team will submit its report after the investigation. Farmers said - National Anthem never happens here Farmer Amar Singh, standing with BJP leader Durgesh Pradhan, said - I went to the school, saw children playing there. I asked the teachers, and they said, "Is this the only work we have left? The government has given us other tasks too." I frequent this school, but I have never heard the National Anthem being played. 'Jana Gana Mana' never happens here, 'Vande Mataram' never happens. When I came on January 26, I couldn't even hear the children's voices. Children's statements from the school The girl said - there is nothing like Hindu-Muslim here After this, our team reached the school. The villagers had gathered on the campus. The police were also there, and children who had come to school had left their classes and come out. They didn't quite know what the whole matter was about? We asked some questions to Priyanshi, who studies in Class 5. She said - Sir never taught anything wrong. He teaches very well. There was no talk of Hindu-Muslim here. The national anthem is also sung every day. When we asked her to recite the national anthem, Priyanshi also recited a part of the national anthem on camera. Girl said - this is all wrong, sir teaches well... Here we met another girl. We asked - how does sir teach? The girl says - he teaches very well, I have never heard him say that Hinduism is wrong. Nor does he talk about anyone. After this, we asked the entire group of children - how does sir teach? To this, everyone smiled and said that sir teaches well. Now, let's talk about the villagers whose children study in this school I come to drop off my nephews, the national anthem is sung every day A large number of parents had also reached the campus. Praveen Kumar, who lives 300 meters away from the school, says - it's just a political matter, there's nothing like that. My 2 sons study in this school. I come to drop off the children at this school every day. The national anthem is also sung here, and classes are held every day. Woman said - Sir is God for children Pooja, a woman living near the school, says - I had gone to the temple. There I found out that Sir has been suspended. As soon as I heard this, I didn't go home, I came straight here. My children studied here. Sir taught them, which is why they always came 1st or 2nd. He is God for the children, he is being defamed. Farmers said - The school has nothing to do with the allegations Farmer Indrapal says - The master's behavior is very good. My daughter and son are doing BSc. Both have studied from here. These allegations have nothing to do with the school. He doesn't differentiate between Hindu-Muslim. On January 26, we villagers are invited. The national anthem is sung, and boondi is distributed. Sanjay said- CCTV in school, everyone is monitored Sanjay Pandey from the village says- This is just a political matter. My house is near this school. My 2 nephews study in this school. I come to school daily to drop them off. The national anthem is sung here daily. Now you see that the complainants are not even from the town. They are outsiders. These people are spoiling the village's atmosphere. CCTVs are installed in this school, their every move is monitored. How will they make them offer Namaz here? No boundary in the school, headmaster was getting it built, this was the root of the dispute Rajan, who lives in the village, says - There is no boundary in this school. You people can see what is happening here as you come and go? Never seen anyone offering Namaz. The headmaster sir was trying to get the boundary wall of this school built. There is a dispute over some part of the land next to the school. Those people are not allowing the boundary to be built there. We feel that these very people conspired with people from the neighboring village and filed a complaint. Now the headmaster sir has been suspended. Now, the school staff speaks Teacher said- I have been teaching since 2014, the headmaster was posted here even before me Understanding the concerns of the children and parents, we entered the school. A teacher was seen standing here. She said- I have been teaching in the school since 2014. The headmaster is indeed Muslim, but you wouldn't be able to tell just by looking at him. He was posted here even before my posting. Teacher Kamna Agarwal said- Sir never discriminated. Whether it was distributing food, teaching children in school, or working in the social sector, he actively participated in all. From his speech, gestures, and behavior, it doesn't seem like he is Muslim. He behaves like an elder of the family. Teacher said - there was also a dispute about SIR here, then only suspension came Assistant teacher Lakshmi said - he always respects women. If there was ever a delay in work, sir would send us first and then go himself. Then Lakshmi said in a hushed voice that I was involved in the SIR process. I have mostly Muslim voters. Some people came and asked to file an objection through Form-7. On this, I asked the officials and they said that a maximum of 10 forms can be given. I told those people to take 10 forms. Later, who knows what they thought? After this, these allegations and the news of the headmaster's suspension came directly. Lakshmi said that the complainants are not residents of this village. They can see the condition of this school. But, those living around this school know nothing. Talk to everyone, no one will speak against the headmaster. Read the Headmaster's Statement Who are the accusers, I don't even know them Headmaster Jan Mohammad was not in school. After being suspended, his health deteriorated. He had gone to Agra to be with his family. We tried to understand the matter from him over the phone. He says - I am a resident of Ram Nagla village in Nauhjheel. I have 2 daughters, 1 son. I don't know why such allegations are being made? I have always considered all children studying in school to be the same. Who are the people making these allegations? I don't even know them. After I recover, I will go to the officials.

stories.title: 'Kanshiram Saheb's ailment... I can't forget that night of 1991':Naseemuddin Siddiqui says, 'To defeat BJP, strategy must be found to counter its influence effectively'
stories.summary: Former minister Naseemuddin Siddiqui, who recently resigned from Congress, recalled a vivid memory from 1991 with BSP founder Kanshiram. He recounted staying with Kanshiram at the old PWD guesthouse in Fatehpur. “It was around 2 a.m., and I woke to hear him pacing and coughing. When I asked about his health, he said, ‘I can’t sleep. Medicine won’t help. First, understand my mission.’” Kanshiram told him, "Every night at 2 a.m., I wake up thinking: I could not make the oppressed society rulers, as Dr. Ambedkar intended. Can I achieve this in my life, or will I leave without accomplishing it?" Siddiqui said the moment left a deep impression on him. “That night shaped my thinking. If Kanshiram could achieve so much, even fulfilling one percent of his mission could elevate the BSP’s cause to new heights.” Siddiqui, who has carved a distinct path in politics, spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about his sudden resignation from Congress ahead of the 2027 UP Assembly elections. He also discussed his next political steps and how he entered politics after leaving the army. Read the full interview for his insights. Q: You were in Congress for eight years. What will be your next political step? A: Leaving Congress was not a one-day decision. I had been considering it for a long time and consulting my team. On January 24, I resigned along with 73 others. Many responsible people were not present that day. I am visiting different districts, seeking advice on whether to join a party or build my own organization. After February 4, I will announce my next political move. Q: You started politics with BSP. Will you return there? A: No. There is no scope for going back to BSP. Once expelled, there is no reason to return. Moreover, I have no intention of going there. Q: You were a sportsman and then in the army. How did you enter politics? A: I joined the army through the sports quota. During my service, my mother had a heart attack and went into a coma. I asked for leave but was denied. I told my superior I would return the same day. He said no, so I resigned and took care of my mother until her final moments. I come from a family of eight siblings; three brothers and one sister have already passed. I first met Kanshiram in 1983–84. Initially, I wasn’t serious about politics and focused on my work. I occasionally attended BSP programs, but became active only from 1989. Q: You were called the “mini CM” in BSP. Can you tell us about that? A: In 1991, I became an MLA. Kanshiram had won a by-election from Etawah. I accompanied him on election campaigns, including a bicycle rally from Saharanpur. We stayed at the old PWD guesthouse in Fatehpur. Kanshiram slept in the large room, and I in the small room beside him. Around 2 a.m., I heard him coughing and pacing. When I asked, he said, “I can’t sleep. Medicine won’t help. First, understand my mission.” He said, “Every night at 2 a.m., I wake up thinking: Ambedkar could not make the oppressed society rulers. Can I achieve this in my life, or will I leave without accomplishing it?” I was moved to tears. That night left a deep impression. If Kanshiram could do so much, even achieving one percent of it could advance our mission for the Bahujan society. Q: Why did BSP’s vote percentage decline continuously? A: There were multiple reasons. Public opinion changes, governments kept shifting between SP, BJP, and our party. Failures are often not pointed out when we are in power. Our opposition, mainly BJP, also adapts strategies, and secular parties should continuously update their tactics. Perhaps we couldn’t fully counter their communal politics, which remains a gap to be filled. Q: Will you form your own party or join another party? A: Both possibilities are under consideration. My goal is not to weaken Congress. I have no personal issue with the party or its leaders. I am consulting people across the state. After February 4, I will announce my next political step. Q: Will you join a grand alliance to defeat BJP? A: I have no personal enmity with BJP, only with its divisive ideology. I oppose anyone who divides society. I believe in brotherhood and secularism, supporting all religions that uphold humanity. Q: How do you view communal issues like the UGC case, Shankaracharya insult, and Brahmin legislators’ meetings? A: When the Supreme Court gave its judgment on Babri Masjid and Ram Janmabhoomi, everyone accepted it. Governments shouldn’t make decisions that insult anyone. Currently, trends influenced by communal forces target communities systematically—first Muslims, now OBCs, tribals, and Dalits. Millions are affected. Politics should not exploit caste or religion to divide citizens. Q: The condition of Muslims has not improved despite different governments. Why? A: A poet once wrote that God never changes the fate of a community that does not care for itself. Politically, Muslims have remained sidelined. Politics is not just about gaining votes in the name of religion; it is about struggle and justice, as shown by leaders and prophets in history. Q: What are your views on the Waqf Amendment Bill? A: The government is attempting to take over properties to benefit industrialists, affecting the poor who live on these lands. Railways, civil aviation, transport, energy—everything has been privatized. Now, historically occupied Waqf lands are being targeted. Governments should protect citizens, not displace them. Q: Looking ahead to the 2027 UP Assembly elections, will BJP retain power or be ousted? A: I wish they could be removed immediately, but it depends on alliances and political equations closer to the elections. The assembly results will come in March 2027. Right now, it’s premature to predict outcomes.

stories.title: ‘We are lion-hearted children…’:CM Yogi smiles on hearing the poem; little Anabia assured of admission | VIDEO
stories.summary: A heartwarming moment unfolded at the Chief Minister’s public hearing in Lucknow when a young girl, Anabia Ali, made a simple but earnest request to Yogi Adityanath. “I want admission in Loreto School, that’s why I came to meet the Chief Minister with my mother. The CM has said that my admission will happen,” Anabia told those present. Standing confidently before the Chief Minister, the little girl folded her hands and said, “Please get me admitted.” Her innocent appeal drew smiles across the hall, including from Yogi Adityanath himself. Amused by her confidence, the Chief Minister asked gently, “Which class do you want admission in?” Without hesitation, Anabia replied, “Nursery, sir.” The brief exchange, marked by warmth and simplicity, quickly caught public attention. The Chief Minister’s affectionate response and the child’s candid request have since gone viral, with many praising the humane moments seen during the public grievance hearing. Watch the video to see the Chief Minister’s unique and gentle interaction with the young petitioner.

stories.title: Man in extramarital affair kills Mumbai live-in partner in Gorakhpur:Love rekindled after 9 years, pressure over child’s identity; double life exposed
stories.summary: Mumbai’s Priya Shetty (35) was brutally murdered in Gorakhpur, allegedly by the man she once loved and lived with. What began as a workplace romance ended in a crime marked by betrayal, secrecy and irreversible consequences. Vijay Kumar Sahani, Priya’s first partner and the father of her son, distanced himself from her barely a year after she gave birth. The emotional rift deepened so sharply that for nearly nine years, the two remained completely absent from each other’s lives. During this period, Vijay remarried. He married Sandhya and became the father of two daughters. In 2022, he moved back to Mumbai with his wife and children and enrolled both daughters in a reputed convent school. It was here that his past resurfaced. Vijay reconnected with Priya through Instagram. The two began meeting again and soon started living together. However, the relationship was fraught with pressure. Priya insisted on two things: that their son be given his father’s name, and that he be admitted to a good convent school. Vijay, who had concealed his first marriage and child from his second family, feared exposure. Determined to keep his double life hidden, he allegedly took Priya nearly 1,680 km away from Mumbai to Gorakhpur—where he murdered her. In this love story, Priya’s son was denied his rightful identity, while Vijay’s own life unravelled completely. Mistakes made during and after the murder led the police to him. Vijay, his wife Sandhya, and his father-in-law have all been arrested and sent to jail. What follows is the chilling story of love, abandonment and murder. Love at an insurance office, followed by a year-long live-in relationship Vijay Kumar Sahani, a resident of Madar village in the Sahjanwa area of Gorakhpur, was academically bright from a young age. He had been living in Mumbai’s Charkop area of Kandivali for several years, where he completed his schooling and later graduated in commerce while staying with his elder brother. In 2012, Vijay began working as an agent with HDFC Life Insurance. Around the same time, Priya Shetty joined the office following a vacancy. Their acquaintance soon turned into friendship, and within a month, the two grew emotionally close. Vijay was deeply drawn to Priya. He rented a house, and the two began living together in a live-in relationship. For about a year, they lived harmoniously. During this time, Priya became pregnant. Vijay then married her at a temple, after which Priya began wearing sindoor in his name. In 2013, Priya gave birth to a son, with Vijay by her side. However, soon after the child’s birth, Vijay’s behaviour began to change. He grew distant and increasingly disinterested in Priya. Minor disagreements escalated into frequent arguments. One day, Vijay left the house and moved elsewhere. Acting on the advice of acquaintances, he filed for divorce in an attempt to sever all ties with Priya permanently. A court notice was sent to Priya’s address, but by then she had already vacated the rented house. As a result, the divorce proceedings stalled midway. What remained unresolved then would resurface years later—with fatal consequences. The story of Vijay's return to Gorakhpur and second marriage After 2 years Vijay came home and married Sandhya as his second wife After the year 2013, Vijay had no contact with Priya. Now he felt that she had left his life forever. He came to his village in 2014. Here his family arranged his marriage. In 2015, he married Sandhya from Pipiganj. Both started living happily together. Vijay and Sandhya had 2 daughters. During this time, Vijay's job continued in Mumbai. He made good progress in the insurance sector. Gradually, he reached a monthly salary of 1.5 lakhs. In 2019, Vijay came to the village and started working in insurance from here. In 2022, he decided that he would go back to Mumbai with Sandhya and both daughters and live there. Then he went back to Mumbai. Here he got both daughters admitted to a convent school. Rented a house in a good colony. This way he started living a happy married life. Old love returns to Priya's life, pressure builds on Vijay Vijay started giving money for his son, then they started living together One day while working in office, Vijay saw one of Priya's reels on Instagram. He messaged to ask about her well-being. This is where their conversation started again. Vijay learned that his son was now 9 years old. He also found out that Priya's financial condition was not good. She works as a cook in people's homes to run her household. Then Vijay started giving money to Priya for his son. Priya used to drink a lot of alcohol. So soon she started inviting Vijay to her house too. Vijay and Priya both started drinking and living together at home. Sandhya slowly started finding out about all this, because Vijay wouldn't return home for many days at a time. Sandhya found out about Priya from Vijay's mobile phone. Vijay also didn't want to deceive Sandhya anymore. So he arranged a meeting between both women. However, this made the situation even worse. The final conflict began over children's future According to police, Sandhya's children were studying in private school, while Priya's son was in government school. The dispute escalated over children's rights and future. In 2025, Sandhya told this to her father Rambilas. After this, everyone said okay, you people are alone there. Do one thing, bring Priya to Gorakhpur. The family will sit here and decide what to do next. Murder conspiracy planned by calling to Gorakhpur All three arrived in Gorakhpur by train 4 days before the incident on January 26. Spent the first day at platform number-1. The next day, visited Budhiya Mai place and Gorakhnath temple. Then Vijay drank alcohol with Sandhya and Priya in the hotel room. Vijay had brought 8 bottles of alcohol. After this, everyone reached Pipiganj by auto, where Sandhya's in-laws live. There was a dispute with the auto driver here. After this, they left the auto there. When Sandhya called home, a family member gave them her father's scooter. All three were seen going on this same scooter in the station road CCTV. Around 10 pm, all three left for Sahjanwa on the scooter. On the way, Priya started creating a scene in an intoxicated state. During this time, Vijay and Sandhya planned to kill her instead of taking her home. They murdered Priya by strangling her while she was unconscious from intoxication at a deserted location. However, both were afraid of getting caught. Therefore, Vijay removed all items from Priya's body that could identify her. That's why the police found Priya's body nude. He struck her face 8 to 10 times with a brick to disfigure it. After this, Vijay came to his in-laws' house with his wife. The next morning, Vijay got his facial beard and head hair removed. So that even if his face appeared somewhere in CCTV, he wouldn't be recognized. Now the story of the arrest Auto driver gave first clue to police SP North Gyanendra Prasad said - On January 30, a nude body of a woman was found under the Barghatta bridge in Pipiganj. After this, the search for the accused was started with the help of CCTV and surveillance. A police team got busy identifying the woman. Meanwhile, on the night of the incident, 3 people were seen going on a scooter in CCTV. Considering them suspicious, information was gathered about them. The first clue came from an auto driver. Who had seen a man and woman with the deceased. This clue slowly led us to Vijay and Sandhya. Finally, after arresting them, they confessed to their crime. They have been sent to jail.

stories.title: 14-year-old steals ₹85 lakh family jewellery for momos:UP's Deoria teen empties wardrobe; shopkeepers exchange gold for feeding him
stories.summary: A bizarre case has emerged from Deoria, Uttar Pradesh, where a 14-year-old boy reportedly stole jewelry worth Rs 85 lakh over three months to feed his obsession with momos. Each day, he took items from the family almirah and handed them to local shopkeepers, who in return gave him momos. The stolen items included gold necklaces, rings, bangles, earrings, and silver anklets, which were given to three shopkeepers. Discovery leaves family shocked The case came to light on Sunday, when the boy’s aunt opened the family almirah to collect some jewelry and found it empty. Shocked, the family questioned the boy, who confessed to giving the items to the shopkeepers in exchange for momos. Following this, the family filed a police complaint against the minor and the three accused shopkeepers. On Monday evening, police registered a case and arrested one of the accused, who is currently being interrogated. The case falls under the Rampur Karkhana police jurisdiction. How the theft happened The victim’s father, Vimlesh Mishra, a temple priest from Bhagwanpur Tiwari village, said his son studies locally. The boy developed a habit of eating momos, which was exploited by three young men running a momo stall at Dumri Chauraha on Deoria–Kasya road. The accused allegedly lured the boy with free momos, persuading him to hand over jewelry from the family almirah daily. List of stolen jewellery The missing items included: The total estimated value of the stolen items is approximately ₹85 lakh. Accused claims jewellery returned One of the accused, Rakesh, claimed that all the jewellery had been returned. He said, “The family is claiming four bangles, but we took only two. We recorded a video of the items and stored them at one location, which was later handed over to the police.” Police action According to Station House Officer Devendra Singh, a case has been registered against the minor and the three shopkeepers—Deepak Kumar, Rakesh, and Pintu. Rakesh has been arrested and is being questioned, while police are actively searching for the other two accused.

stories.title: Rain hits 10 districts in UP, hailstorms in 4 regions:Yogi asks officials to assess damage; 6 fog-related crashes, 15 vehicles collide
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh has taken a sudden turn for the worse. In Lucknow and Kanpur, darkness descended during the daytime as drizzle was accompanied by strong, storm-like winds. Hoardings and tin sheds along roads collapsed, and several areas experienced waterlogging. In the early hours of Tuesday, heavy rainfall was recorded in 10 districts, including Auraiya and Jalaun. In Unnao, Chitrakoot, Hardoi, and Etawah, hail fell for about half an hour, covering roads with a white layer of ice. Standing crops in fields were damaged, and residents stayed indoors. Those venturing outside for essential work were seen relying on umbrellas and raincoats. See weather pictures- Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to assess the damage caused by the unseasonal rains. Meanwhile, dense fog has settled over 20 districts, including Aligarh, Mainpuri, and Bulandshahr, reducing visibility in some areas to near zero. Road, rail, and air traffic have been severely affected. Over 25 trains are running late at several railway stations, including Lucknow, while flights at airports are departing with delays. In six districts, including Unnao, 15 vehicles collided due to slippery conditions. In Pilibhit, a truck ran over a farmer. On the Agra Expressway, a bus carrying passengers collided with a truck, leaving several people injured. According to the Meteorological Department, the late-night interaction between a western disturbance and an anticyclone has led to the formation of cloud clusters, resulting in rainfall. Agricultural expert Siddharth Singh stated that the strong winds, rain, and hail have caused damage to wheat and sugarcane crops, while mustard and vegetable crops have also started to rot. Senior scientist from Lucknow, Atul Kumar Singh, said: "The heavy snowfall in Uttarakhand and Nepal is directly affecting the Terai and plains districts of Uttar Pradesh. Due to the impact of a new western disturbance, the drizzle that began in western UP has now spread to Bundelkhand, the Vindhya region, and the Prayagraj division. This weather pattern is expected to continue until February 4. After that, the fog will clear, and temperatures will drop slightly."

stories.summary: A fight and stone-pelting occurred between students of two hostels at BHU (Banaras Hindu University) on Thursday. In the incident, PG student Piyush Tiwari sustained serious head injuries. He has been referred to the Trauma Center. It is alleged that expelled students Darshit Pandey, Raunak Mishra, Ankit Pal, and Vishwajeet Yadav assaulted Piyush Tiwari at the gate of Ruiya Hostel. After the incident, there was chaos in the hostel. Upon receiving information, Inspector Lanka Rajkumar Sharma and BHU Outpost In-charge Saurabh Tiwari arrived at the scene with forces. They pacified the agitated students. The agitated students are demanding action against the accused. Seeing the students' anger, 500 policemen, including DCP Kashi Gaurav, are conducting a search operation in the hostel. Surveillance is being done with drones. One fleeing student has been apprehended and taken for questioning. According to the Chief Proctor, 11 rooms of Birla-C Hostel have been sealed. Some suspicious items have also been found here. 4 pictures

stories.title: Bully drives gypsy with man on bonnet for 15 minutes:Starts spinning vehicle as people chase him in Rampur; video surfaces
stories.summary: In Rampur, a youth drove a Gypsy with an e-rickshaw driver stuck on its bonnet for about 200 metres, even spinning the vehicle in circles as people chased him to rescue the victim. The incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon at Kemri Tirahe on the Bilaspur Highway, and a video has surfaced. The speeding Gypsy had first hit the e-rickshaw, injuring the driver. When the injured man stood in front of the vehicle to stop it, the driver instead accelerated, throwing him onto the bonnet and driving for nearly 15 minutes before stopping. Police have registered a case against the accused Gypsy driver. 3 pictures Read the full story Police sent the accused to ADM Court The e-rickshaw driver could have lost his life in the incident, but instead of taking strict action, the police took action under the section for disturbing the peace. Driving a vehicle negligently and endangering life (Rash Driving) falls under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which carries a punishment of up to 6 months in jail or a fine. In this case, Kotwali Station House Officer Balwan Singh informed that the arrested accused is Manpreet Singh, a resident of Sant Colony locality in the city. Action has been taken against him under sections for disturbing the peace. He has been sent to the SDM Court.

stories.title: Setback for Brij Bhushan Singh:Delhi High Court pulls up counsel, allows trial court hearing to go on, trouble deepens for former MP
stories.summary: The troubles of Uttar Pradesh strongman leader and former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh have not eased. In the sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers, the Delhi High Court on Thursday ruled that the trial court proceedings will continue and refused to stay the hearing. The court also reprimanded Brij Bhushan Singh’s counsel during the proceedings. Brij Bhushan Singh had approached the Delhi High Court seeking a stay on the trial court proceedings related to the FIR and charges framed against him. However, a bench headed by Justice Swarna Kanta Sharma declined to grant any interim relief and directed that the matter continue in the lower court. The High Court has now listed the case for further hearing on April 21. Brij Bhusan's lawyer sought adjournment During the hearing, Brij Bhushan Singh’s lawyer sought an adjournment, citing the absence of the main counsel. The court, however, rejected the request and made it clear that the trial should proceed without delay. The case is currently being heard at the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi. Court expressed displeasure with lawyer Justice Swarna Kanta said- Why haven't you been arguing until now? You have filed this petition, but it hasn't been presented for argument even once so far. Brijbhushan's lawyer assured the court that at the next hearing they will present their senior lawyer in court for arguments. The court warned that if there is no argument at the next hearing, the petition could be dismissed. The court said, ‘It is clarified that there is no stay on trial court proceedings.’ Brij Bhushan's claim - False allegations were made Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh had said in the High Court in 2024 that he was implicated in false allegations. He alleged that the investigation was biased and only the statements of the victims were given importance, while the truth of the allegations was not investigated. FIR was registered on Supreme Court's order In May 2023, Delhi Police registered an FIR against Brij Bhushan after Supreme Court's intervention. On May 21, 2024, the trial court framed charges against him for sexual harassment, criminal intimidation and outraging the modesty of women. Co-accused and former WFI Assistant Secretary Vinod Tomar was also charged with criminal intimidation. 6 wrestlers made allegations On January 18, 2023, 6 wrestlers made sexual harassment allegations against former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. The women wrestlers demanded action against Brij Bhushan from Union Sports Minister Anurag Thakur. When no action was taken at the government level in this matter, male and female wrestlers held a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar for more than six months. Acquitted in sexual exploitation case of minor wrestler Delhi's Patiala House Court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual exploitation case of a minor wrestler on May 26, 2025, and closed the case. In this case, the minor had retracted from her statement. After which the court took this decision. After the sexual exploitation case was closed, Brij Bhushan's close associates celebrated in Gonda. During the in-camera hearing on August 1, 2023, the minor had said that she made these allegations under political or emotional pressure. No such incident had occurred where she considered herself a victim. After this statement, the court considered it as 'serious variable evidence'. Brij Bhushan had said - There was no truth in the case Dainik Bhaskar had spoken to former MP Brij Bhushan over phone about the court's decision. He had said - This is the blessing of Bajrangbali and Lord Ram that I got my first major victory in this case. The minor wrestler had made allegations against me due to instigation by alleged wrestlers. But when she learned the truth, she gave the correct statement. Based on which the court has dismissed that case.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Supreme Court stays UGC's new regulations Supreme Court put a hold on the University Grants Commission (UGC)’s new rules until further orders. The bench of CJI Suryakant and Justice Joymalya said the provisions are unclear and could be misused. 2. UP cabinet approves cashless healthcare for 10 lakh teachers Ahead of Assembly elections, the UP Cabinet approved a cashless healthcare scheme for over 10 lakh teachers and education staff, including Shiksha Mitras, with a treatment limit of ₹5 lakh. The decision was taken in a Cabinet meeting chaired by CM Yogi Adityanath, which cleared 29 major proposals. 3. Elderly man commits suicide over unpaid electricity bill in Shahjahanpur An elderly man allegedly died by suicide over unpaid electricity dues of ₹32,000 in Shahjahanpur. A handwritten note addressed to CM Yogi Adityanath requested a waiver of his bills and asked authorities not to trouble his children after his death. 4. Ajit Pawar cremated in Maharashtra's Baramati with full-state honours Ajit Pawar was cremated with full state honours at Vidya Pratishthan ground, Baramati, around 12:15 pm on Thursday. His family, including wife Sunetra, sons Parth and Jai, Sharad Pawar, and Supriya Sule attended. Political leaders present included Amit Shah, Nitin Gadkari and Raj Thackeray. 5. Two prisoners escape Ayodhya jail after wall breach Two inmates in a special cell of Ayodhya District Jail escaped overnight by uprooting 30 bricks, triggering a major security alert. Following the incident, seven officials, including the jailer, were suspended. 6. Administration shuts 30 spa centres after Gorakhpur gangrape Following the gangrape of a 13-year-old girl in Gorakhpur, authorities suspended six police officers and shut down 30 illegal spa centres. The girl had posted an Instagram reel before leaving her colony, prompting swift action against the exploitation network. 7. India's GDP growth projected at 6.8-7.2% for FY27 Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Economic Survey 2025-26 in Parliament on 29 January 2026. The survey estimates India’s GDP growth at 6.8-7.2% for FY27, slightly lower than the 7.4% projected for the current fiscal year, according to sources. 8. Shankaracharya leaves Magh Mela suddenly after conflict with administration Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati abruptly left the Magh Mela on January 28 after an 11-day conflict with the Prayagraj administration. Officials said a closed-door meeting was held hours earlier; they expressed regret, but the Shankaracharya insisted on an apology before leaving. 9. Rs 71 lakh fraud in Kanpur fake IAS marriage case In Kanpur, a man posed as a bank officer and claimed to be selected for IAS, luring a young woman with marriage promises. He extorted about ₹71 lakh, including cash and jewelry, before being caught and sent to jail. 10. Jamaat leader dies in B'desh pre-election clash with BNP activists A Jamaat-e-Islami leader died at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital after being injured in a clash with BNP activists in Sherpur. The deceased, Maulana Md Rezaul Karim was the secretary of Jamaat’s Sreebordi upazila unit.

stories.title: Youth run over by Thar in Lucknow:Leg fractured from 3 places, accused out on bail within 1 day, victim says, 'They wanted to kill me'
stories.summary: A shocking incident came to light in Lucknow where a young businessman was brutally assaulted in front of a police post following a minor dispute. The accused allegedly knocked the victim to the ground, ran a Thar SUV over him, and deliberately left the vehicle stationary on his body for several minutes. Eyewitnesses said the victim lay trapped under the vehicle, groaning in pain, while the accused refused to move the Thar forward. As a result of the assault, the businessman’s leg was fractured at three places, leaving him unable to walk. He later lost consciousness and regained it only during treatment at the hospital. The victim’s friend, who was present at the scene, also sustained serious injuries to his head and ears and is currently undergoing medical treatment. Both accused out on bail in 1 day The incident occurred on the night of January 22 in the parking area of the Summit Building. Despite the gravity of the incident, both accused were granted bail within a day. Initially, police invoked sections related to breach of peace, though a case has also been registered under attempt to murder provisions. Speaking to Bhaskar, the victim alleged that the attackers kept the Thar parked on top of him for nearly 25 minutes, worsening his injuries. Police officials said the matter is under investigation, and statements of the victims and witnesses have been recorded. See pictures... Read sequence of events... Pawan Patel, originally from Fatehpur, currently resides in New Gudora in Sarojininagar and runs a building material business. He told Bhaskar that a few of his friends had come from the village, and at their request, he took them out for a late-night outing on January 22. According to Pawan, the group was partying at King Club in the Summit Building along with his friend Prashant Sachan and others. At around 1 am, when they stepped out of the parking area to leave in their cars, they noticed a group of youths in a Thar SUV and another car arguing among themselves on the premises. Pawan said he tried to intervene and calm the situation along with his friends. However, this reportedly angered the youths, who began abusing and assaulting them. During the altercation, the accused allegedly attempted to snatch Prashant Sachan’s chain and then ran the Thar over him. Bullies kept Thar mounted for 25 minutes Pawan said that during the scuffle with Prashant, he somehow managed to move away from the spot to save himself. Meanwhile, other companions arrived and tried to understand and defuse the situation, but the accused youths continued abusing them. Fearing further violence, Pawan and his friends ran outside to seek help. He said they asked the security guard to close the gate. At that moment, the Thar driven by the accused allegedly rammed into them from behind, causing him to fall to the ground. The assailants then reversed the vehicle and deliberately ran it over him. According to Pawan, the Thar remained parked on both his legs for nearly 25 minutes, during which he cried out in pain. He eventually lost consciousness and does not recall what happened next. He regained consciousness only after being admitted to the hospital. Leg bone broken from 3 places Pawan said that in the incident, his leg bone was broken from 3 places. It has a temporary plaster cast. The other leg also has serious injuries. That leg remains swollen. He is walking with the help of a walker. Doctors have advised to apply permanent plaster after 4 days. We were beaten up in someone else's dispute Pawan's friend Prashant Sachan said that they were returning after a party. Two groups were having a dispute on the way. There was difficulty in passing through there. When we objected to this, the bullies attacked us. We came out from a different club and the accused boys came from another club. They started fighting with people to take revenge for someone else's dispute. The goons came in two cars. There was also a Swift Dzire involved in the incident. The Thar was stopped by closing the gate but the Dzire occupants escaped. Police arrested Akash Yadav and Mohit Mewadi, residents of Rudrapur, Uttarakhand, from the spot. Questions raised on police working style There is a police post adjacent to gate number 4 of the Summit Building, which would be barely 30 meters from the incident site. Despite this, the accused had no fear. The parking dispute continued for about half an hour, but the police didn't even know about it. However, police claim that the club is closed at 12 AM. The internal security clears the entire parking from 12:30 to 1 AM. This incident has raised questions about police functioning. Inspector Vibhutikhand Amar Singh said that a report has been filed based on the victim's complaint. The Thar used in the incident has been seized. Raids are being conducted to search for other absconding accused.

stories.title: 'Keshav Maurya failed to take a stand' says Avimukteshwaranand:Shankaracharya questions govt silence over Magh Mela incident
stories.summary: 'If someone says they will go only when they are sent, it means they lack independent judgement. A discerning person takes decisions by assessing the situation themselves. Here, government representatives should have taken a clear stand, which they failed to do.' These remarks were made by Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati after returning to Kashi from Prayagraj, while speaking to the media. He was responding to a statement made by Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya during the Magh Mela protest. The Deputy CM had said that the Chief Minister had taken cognisance of the matter and that he would speak when asked, pray if required, and bow at the feet if needed. ‘Insult to Shankaracharya is direct insult to Sanatan’ The Shankaracharya referred to Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s statement that governments which insult Sanatan do not return to power. He said that in Prayagraj, Brahmacharis, Batuks, saints, householders, and devotees who came for Sangam Snan were insulted. Since the Shankaracharya himself represents Sanatan, his humiliation amounts to a direct insult to Sanatan Dharma. He added that had the government abandoned its arrogance and corrected its mistake in time, the situation would not have escalated. Akhilesh Yadav’s statement shows issue goes beyond religion Commenting on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s remarks, the Shankaracharya said that when political leaders themselves are calling the incident unfortunate, it is clear that the matter is not merely religious but is also linked to governance and sensitivity. ‘Denial of Sangam Snan Was Unthinkable’ Avimukteshwaranand described his inability to take the Sangam Snan as unfortunate and unimaginable. He said that despite being given opportunities continuously for 11 days, the failure to correct the mistake was deeply distressing. He explained that in Sanatan tradition, a yagna is not considered complete until the Purnahuti is performed. It was traditionally believed that the collective snan of Sanatan followers is completed only after the Shankaracharya’s snan. This time, he said, the Purnahuti did not take place. See 3 photos- ‘UGC’s new act will divide society’ Upon arriving in Kashi, the Shankaracharya performed formal worship at the Math and held an important meeting with the saint community. Serious discussions took place on the cow protection movement and recent developments. Speaking on the controversy related to the UGC, he said it is not an issue of any single political party but one that divides society. Pitting one caste against another and encouraging internal conflict weakens Hindu society. He alleged that what is said on public platforms is contradicted by actual conduct. 'On stage, slogans like ‘Bantoge toh katoge’ are raised, but in practice, machines to divide and destroy are being brought in,' he said. ‘Governments not serious about stopping cow slaughter’ The Shankaracharya said that governments at both the Centre and state levels are not serious about stopping cow slaughter. He alleged that those who raise the issue are deliberately silenced. He clearly stated that Sanatan tradition is not run by any government, leader, or political party. “Attempts will be made to silence us, but we will not stop. Every Sanatani must now join the movement to protect Gomata. We are not concerned with who is in power or which party governs,” he said. ‘Allegations must be proven, mere claims are not enough’ Avimukteshwaranand said that organisations like the Vishva Hindu Raksha Parishad had put up posters against him in Raebareli, calling him a ‘Kalyugi Ravan’ and even a Pakistani agent. He said such allegations must be proven, as mere statements mean nothing. He added that whatever he says is backed by logic and evidence. Questions raised on police action and lack of inquiry Referring to the Magh Mela unrest, he said the complete truth has still not emerged and the public has seen only a fraction of what happened. Had the full video surfaced, the picture would have been entirely different. Questioning the police role, he asked whether reprimanding one policeman and suspending another amounts to justice. He pointed out that no independent inquiry committee was formed. Anger over silence of centre and state governments On the question of central intervention, he said that when something is wrong, hierarchy becomes irrelevant. Right must be called right and wrong must be called wrong, but in this case, no one is speaking. He said that after the incident, he waited peacefully for 11 days, hoping corrective action would be taken. He believed initially it might have been a local administrative lapse, but no concrete action followed even after such a serious matter. Clarification on unity of 4 Shankaracharyas Addressing confusion regarding the unity of the four Shankaracharyas, Avimukteshwaranand said a false narrative is being spread that they are divided. He asserted that all four Shankaracharyas have always been united. He said those claiming otherwise are spreading misinformation. In the recent events, all four Shankaracharyas stood together. He emphasised that Shankaracharyas hold the highest position in Sanatan tradition and their role should not be undermined. Call for probe into Maharashtra Plane Crash On the death of Ajit Pawar in the Maharashtra plane crash, the Shankaracharya said such tragic incidents must be investigated impartially and thoroughly. He said the nature of the inquiry should ensure the truth comes out and no confusion or suspicion remains. What has happened so far?

stories.title: Jaish-e-Mohammed, Al-Qaeda linked terrorist drew up hit list of 7:People from Delhi UP included in list, police procure weapons for public killings
stories.summary: On January 25, 2026, Gujarat ATS arrested a suspicious youth from the Charpul area of Navsari. The arrested accused was identified as Faizan Sheikh, who is originally from Rampur, Uttar Pradesh and was currently living in Navsari, where he worked as a tailor. Faizan Sheikh had come under the influence of terrorist organizations and was planning to spread terror in the country. For this, he had also purchased a pistol and six cartridges. Faizan Sheikh had prepared a list of people who made statements against Islam and the Prophet and planned to kill them. Faizan had made a list of seven people, which has been obtained by ATS. Faizan had also made controversial posts about killing these seven people in such a way that the world would watch. Literature of 29 pages found in Urdu and Arabic language Faizan was also in contact with terrorists from terrorist organizations like Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba and admitted that he was ready to carry out any incident at their direction. However, ATS caught him before this intention could be fulfilled. Literature of 29 pages in Urdu and Arabic language was also recovered from him. Faizan made a list of seven people ATS begins investigation of Faizan's phone details Along with this, the list was also forwarded in a specific group and mentioned that these people would be killed in a way for the world to see. Additionally, the ATS team has started investigating all the details of Faizan's phone. They have begun a detailed investigation of who he was connected with on social media. Was influenced by radical ideology of Jaish-e-Mohammed and Al-Qaeda ATS investigation has revealed that Faizan Sheikh was influenced by the radical ideology of banned terrorist organizations Jaish-e-Mohammed and Al-Qaeda. After being radicalized through online media and other means, he had targeted specific groups of people with the intention of spreading fear and creating chaos in society. Gujarat ATS reached where the terrorist was picked up from. During his interrogation, it was found that he was following Masood Azhar and was collecting data on those who made statements against the Prophet. He had bought weapons from the money he earned by sewing clothes. Accused prepared a list of prominent people from UP The accused was associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed group. He had been living in Navsari for the last 4 years and worked as a tailor. He was running groups on Instagram and Telegram. The accused had started targeting people who spoke against Prophet Mohammed. The accused had prepared a list of prominent people from UP. The accused has not attacked anyone so far. The accused used to follow terrorist Masood Azhar A person named Abu Bakar was associated with the accused, who is under investigation. The accused used to make plans on Instagram and Telegram to kill those who spoke against the Prophet and would share these plans with others. The accused also used to follow terrorist Masood Azhar. He would collect online data of people who made statements against the Prophet. Faizan Sheikh had been working as a tailor in Navsari for the past few years Faizan Sheikh was currently living in the Charpul area of Navsari and is originally from Dundawala, Narpat Nagar in Rampur district of Uttar Pradesh. He had been earning his livelihood by working as a tailor in Navsari for the past few years, where large-scale job work is done and craftsmen from Uttar Pradesh work.

stories.title: Fake IAS cheats woman of ₹71 lakh in Kanpur:Accused Nitesh Pandey promises marriage and blackmails her, takes jewellery and cash; arrested
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a cunning young man first trapped a young woman in a love affair by introducing himself as a government bank officer. After this, he claimed to have been selected for IAS. He lured the girl with the promise of marriage. He said that he needed millions of rupees for the selection and asked for money. On this, the girl gave him about 71 lakh rupees, including cash and jewelry. The cunning young man assured her of joining IAS by sending fake emails, joining letters, and documents on WhatsApp from a mail ID similar to a government department's website. Police have arrested the accused Nitesh Pandey. Know the full case in detail Took ₹ 26.50 lakh cash and ₹45 lakh worth of Jewelry The young woman residing in Kalyanpur used to work in a media organization. Her father is a clerk in the municipal corporation. She has two brothers. Her mother has passed away. Her brothers run a shop under the name Mamta Artificial. After her mother's death, the girl herself used to keep the house's money and jewelry etc. The girl's brother said - money had been collected and kept for the shop and his sister's wedding. The jewelry was also with his sister. Cunning Nitesh Pandey gave the pretext of marriage. He demanded millions of rupees in the name of selection in IAS. The sister gave the jewelry and cash kept at home. Nitesh first took 26.50 lakh rupees in cash. After this, he also swindled gold and silver jewelry worth approximately 45 lakh rupees. The victim girl said - Diwakar Mishra alias Satyam of Shuklaganj is a family friend. Through him, she met Nitesh Pandey, a resident of Chakeri. Nitesh first introduced himself as a Field Officer in a government bank, then claimed to be an SDM, and later claimed selection in IAS. The young man started distancing himself after taking money Nitesh deceived her, saying he would marry her after completing his IAS training. Therefore, the girl completely trusted him. The young man gradually started distancing himself. When she became suspicious and asked for her money back, he procrastinated by giving a fake check. Threatened with a knife, said he would implicate her in a false case It is alleged that when the young woman asked for money and threatened to file a police case, the young man Nitesh started blackmailing her. He threatened to kill her. He threatened to viral her private pictures. On October 14, 2025, the young woman had gone to the house of Diwakar Mishra alias Satyam. It is alleged that here Nitesh Pandey threatened her with a knife. He abused her. He threatened to kill the entire family and implicate them in false cases. FIR against four accused, main accused arrested late at night On the application of the victim girl, Kalyanpur police station registered an FIR against four accused on Wednesday. Police have registered a report against Nitesh Pandey, Diwakar Mishra alias Satyam, Jitesh Pandey and Akanksha Pandey. Accused Nitesh Pandey is an MA pass in Psychology. His father and mother have passed away; his father was retired from the Air Force. He lives with his brother and sister-in-law.

stories.title: Illegal dairy operators hide animals in bedrooms:LMC recovers buffaloes and goats after 3-hour raid in Lucknow
stories.summary: A bizarre scene unfolded in Lucknow when buffaloes and goats were found hidden inside a house’s bedroom during a municipal corporation drive against illegal dairies. The incident occurred in Bijnor area of Zone-8, where a team of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation (LMC) had arrived to take action against unlawfully operating dairy units. As soon as the civic team reached Royal City Colony in Gadora, dairy operators attempted to evade action by locking their animals inside residential houses. In one such case, a dairy owner confined buffaloes and goats inside a room of his house, turning bedrooms and drawing rooms into makeshift cattle shelters. Drive conducted for 3 hours LMC officials faced stiff resistance from locals, and their vehicles were also surrounded during the operation. Despite the obstruction, the team continued the drive and, after nearly three hours of sustained effort, managed to remove the animals from inside the houses. Officials said that several buffaloes and cows were recovered from living spaces, highlighting the extent to which illegal dairy operators had encroached upon residential areas. The action was carried out to curb unhygienic conditions and violations caused by illegal dairies in the locality. See pictures... During the operation, the municipal corporation seized a total of 11 buffaloes, four heifers, three cows and one calf. All the animals have been shifted to the Aishbagh Kanji House, where they will remain detained until the prescribed penalty is paid, officials said. The action was initiated following repeated complaints from local residents, who alleged that illegal dairy operators were dumping animal dung in open plots and discharging waste into sewer lines. This had led to severe filth, waterlogging and an increased risk of mosquito-borne diseases in the area. Buffalo rearing prohibited in city limits The Municipal Corporation clarified that under the Municipal Corporation Act, 1959, rearing of buffaloes is completely banned within urban limits, as buffaloes are classified as pollution-causing animals. As per rules, residents are permitted to keep a maximum of two cows, and that too only with a valid license. Joint operation by multiple departments The enforcement drive was carried out with the joint participation of the police force, municipal enforcement team and the animal welfare department. Animal Welfare Officer Dr Abhinav Verma said that strict action against illegally operating dairies will continue in the coming days. At the spot, special assistance was provided by team members Manoj, Ramkumar, Furkan and Nadeem, who played a key role in successfully carrying out the operation despite resistance.
