stories.title: BSP leader’s Rottweiler attacks child in Hamirpur:Boy bitten on chest and arm, rushed to hospital; police probe, inquiry on dog's licence status
stories.summary: A Rottweiler dog owned by a BSP leader launched a life-threatening attack on a minor child in Hamirpur. The child fell to the ground as the dog attacked him, biting his hand and chest at four places and causing serious injuries. Hearing the child’s screams, the BSP leader rushed to the spot. The child was somehow rescued and immediately admitted to hospital. The 11-year-old had gone to the leader’s house to play with other children. He was coming down the stairs after playing on the terrace when the dog suddenly attacked him. The incident took place on Sunday night in the Sumerpur police station area. Police said a complaint has been received from the family. Preliminary inquiry has revealed that BSP Nagar President Shivam Janardan owns two Rottweiler dogs, neither of which is licensed. Know the full matter Rajendra Kumar Gautam, a resident of Sumerpur town, works in a steel mill. On Sunday evening, his son Ansh went to play at the BSP leader’s house, located about 50 metres away. He played on the terrace with his friend Pathik for around two hours. While returning home, the Rottweiler suddenly pounced on him. Ansh said he did not even get a chance to react. The dog bit him multiple times on his hand and chest. Hearing his cries, the BSP leader and family members reached the spot and rescued the child, but by then he had suffered serious injuries. The injured child was rushed to the Sumerpur Community Health Centre for treatment. Father said - Police did not take action even after complaint The victim’s father Rajendra Kumar said he submitted a written complaint against neighbour Shivam Janardan, but no action has been taken so far. Police said the matter is under investigation based on the complaint. Don't be careless if a dog bites Dr Rohit Bhati said dog bites should never be taken lightly. Rabies is a fatal viral disease that spreads through bites or scratches from dogs, cats or other animals. If anti-rabies injections are not given in time, the virus can spread rapidly and affect the brain, nervous system and heart, which can be fatal. Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of stray dogs According to 2019 data from the Union Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of stray dogs in the country — over 20.5 lakh. In Lucknow alone, surveys estimated between 75,000 and 95,000 stray dogs. Rules for Pet Dogs Rules for Stray Dogs (ABC Program)

stories.title: Human trafficking racket busted near Nepal border:Police rescue four girls being brought at night through dense jungle routes, two traffickers arrested
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Police have busted another gang involved in prostitution and human trafficking in Shravasti district. Four Nepali girls being brought into Uttar Pradesh through dense forest routes along the Nepal border were rescued by the police. Two traffickers were also arrested during the operation. Police said the girls were being brought from Nepal through forest routes late at night after being lured with false promises of work as dancers in orchestras. Acting on a tip-off, the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and local police carried out a joint operation and rescued the girls, who were being transported on two motorcycles. According to police, the girls were extremely frightened. On seeing the police, they panicked and began crying loudly. Female constables present with the rescue team counselled the girls and helped calm them down. It may be noted that Dainik Bhaskar had carried a special investigation report two days earlier exposing the trafficking of underage Nepali girls in the India–Nepal border areas. During the investigation, traffickers and agents had gone on camera explaining how girls are taken from small villages in Nepal and routed through Uttar Pradesh to major Indian cities and even Gulf countries. Following the report’s publication, border police, the SSB and local police had intensified surveillance and operations. Rescue operation in detail On January 31, 2026, Sub-Inspector Deepak Giri of Sirsiya police station was attending a border coordination meeting with the SSB along the India–Nepal border. During the meeting, an informer provided critical information that two Indian youths were bringing four Nepali girls into India via forest routes on motorcycles. Given the seriousness of the information, NGOs and the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) were immediately alerted, and a swift action plan was drawn up. Police teams set up a strategic blockade on the forest route ahead of Bhachkahi village in the Gujjar Gauri border area. Shortly afterwards, two motorcycles carrying two youths and four visibly distressed Nepali girls were spotted. The police intercepted the vehicles and apprehended the youths on the spot, successfully rescuing the four girls from falling into the trafficking network. During questioning, the arrested accused were identified as Hariram Yadav, son of Raksharam, and Ramroop, son of Ram Lotan—both residents of Babhani Kukurbhukva village under Sirsiya police station in Shravasti district. Preliminary investigations revealed that the accused were operating a local human trafficking network along the Nepal border. Police recovered two motorcycles, one Aadhaar card and two mobile phones from their possession. A case has been registered under serious sections related to human trafficking, and both accused have been sent to judicial custody. Police said the role of other members linked to the network is also being investigated. Orchestra lure, plan to send girls to different locations Interrogation revealed that the accused had shown the girls dreams of earning money by dancing in orchestras. In reality, they were preparing to send them to different locations, where the risk of exploitation was evident. SP: Vigilance increased along the border Superintendent of Police Rahul Bhati praised the operation and said the district follows a zero-tolerance policy against human trafficking. Surveillance has been stepped up in border areas, and such networks will be dismantled completely, he said.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to get sewer connections for 3 lakh homes:2,650 km of lines to be laid across 8 zones, ₹2,500 crore project to transform city
stories.summary: Gorakhpur city is set to provide sewer connections to nearly three lakh homes over the next two to three years, transforming the city’s sanitation infrastructure through a ₹2,500 crore sewerage project. The Yogi government has taken several steps in recent years to address the city’s long-standing sewerage problems. Under this initiative, approximately 2,650 kilometres of sewer lines will be laid. Several projects under the plan have already been completed, while others are in progress. Additionally, another project worth ₹721.40 crore has been approved to further expand the sewer network. City divided into 8 zones for sewer development Since taking office, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has focused on improving Gorakhpur’s sewerage system, implementing solutions in multiple phases. The Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation area has been divided into eight zones to streamline the work. Currently, around 2,318 km of sewer lines have been laid or are under construction, with an expenditure of ₹1,858.34 crore. These works are connecting approximately 2.5 lakh homes to the sewer system. Thousands of homes benefiting through AMRUT scheme Under the AMRUT 2.0 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) program: For Zone C-2 Part 2, a project worth ₹561.34 crore is underway, which includes laying 188.47 km of sewer lines and establishing a 30 MLD STP. Once completed by March 2026, this phase will connect 43,963 homes. As of now, about 165 km of sewer lines in this zone have already been laid. Additional projects strengthening sewer infrastructure The Godhoiya Nala project, under AMRUT, involves constructing a 38 MLD STP at a cost of ₹495.24 crore. Meanwhile, the Katniya-Mahewa Nala Interception and Diversion project, costing ₹53.03 crore, includes a 10 MLD STP. The National Lake Conservation Program has also contributed to improving Gorakhpur’s sewerage system. Under this program, ₹196.57 crore projects in Zone A-1 and Zone A-2 have already established 15 MLD and 30 MLD STPs respectively. New project approved to benefit 43,604 homes In a state cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the government approved a ₹721.40 crore project for Gorakhpur Sewerage Scheme Zone A-3. This project will provide sewer connections to 43,604 homes across 17 wards, laying 342.19 km of sewer lines. Once completed, Gorakhpur’s sewer network will extend over 2,500 km, significantly improving sanitation, sewage management, and urban hygiene in the city.

stories.title: Govt teacher forces students to offer Namaz in school:Pressurised students to accept Islam, scolded for reciting national anthem; suspended
stories.summary: A case has come to light from a government school in Mathura where a teacher allegedly forced students to offer Namaz. The teacher is also accused of brainwashing children, compelling them to embrace Islam. He reportedly portrayed Islam as superior to other religions and made disrespectful remarks about Hindu deities. Following a complaint by a BJP leader, the Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) suspended the teacher and formed a two-member committee to investigate. Preliminary inquiry found the teacher’s actions to be true. According to the BJP leader, the children’s parents informed him of the matter. He filed a complaint with the BSA on January 30, and action was taken two days later. The incident occurred at Naujheel Primary School under Manta police station. Motivating children to adopt Islam Durgesh Pradhan, BJP Bazna Mandal president, said the school has both Hindu and Muslim students, with Hindus being the majority. The teacher, identified as Jan Mohammad, reportedly brainwashed children, forcing them to offer Namaz. “He demeaned Hinduism, insulted Hindu gods and goddesses, and invited outsiders from the Tablighi Jamaat to the school to teach Islam,” Pradhan said. “Children were scolded for singing the national anthem and told that Islam is superior to other religions and that they must follow its teachings.” Parents had complained to BJP leader Pradhan added that children, distressed by the teacher’s behaviour, informed their parents, who then brought it to his attention. The parents requested the BSA to investigate and take action against the accused teacher. BSA says - Initial investigation confirms allegations against teacher Ratan Kirti of BSA said that a complaint was received regarding the teacher forcing students to offer Namaz. The Block Education Officer (BEO) submitted a report, which found the teacher prima facie guilty. “Jan Mohammad has been suspended and attached to Nagla Humayun Primary School in Manta. BEOs of Chhata and Manta have been ordered to investigate further. Action will be taken based on their report,” Kirti said.

stories.title: Lucknow residents share views on Union Budget 2026:Experts say it is filled with expectations; professionals argue there is no significant relief
stories.summary: In the 2026 general budget, the central government announced several new schemes. The focus is on making India a medical hub and improving youth skills. Experts say the budget will strengthen the infrastructure sector. However, some people feel it did not meet expectations, as there were hopes for major concessions. There is also no change in the income tax slab. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to selected experts in Lucknow to understand the key points of the budget. Dr. Sanjay Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University, said the budget includes support for caregivers of elderly people. He called this a milestone, as today’s young population will eventually become senior citizens, and this step will help them in the future. He added that the budget includes other long-term benefits. While it may not be called a populist budget, experts agree it will have a significant impact. Dr Singh also highlighted the budget’s focus on science and technology. India’s growing achievements in space technology, he said, show the country’s potential to become a global leader in the coming years. The budget also announces several measures for persons with disabilities, aiming to bring them into the mainstream and allow them to contribute more to the country’s progress. A significant step towards an empowered and prosperous India Acharya Narayan Das of Shri Bharat Milap Ashram, situated in Mayakund, Rishikesh, and a native of Lucknow, says that: The Union Budget of 2026 on India's economic horizon is not merely a simple financial statement, but a strong pillar that will give concrete shape to the vision of 'Developed India'. The soul of this budget lies in the coordination of economic discipline and modern national aspirations. On one hand, the government has controlled the fiscal deficit within the modest limit of 4.3%, while on the other hand, the huge capital allocated for basic infrastructure will accelerate the country's progress. Special emphasis on emerging and strategic sectors like semiconductors and bio-pharma clearly indicates that India is now not just a market for consumption, but is moving towards becoming a global hub for innovation, research, and manufacturing. This budget is free from the allure of momentary populist promises and focuses on long-term and sustainable results. A robust banking system, accessible and inclusive technology, along with these, are important steps towards a self-reliant, capable, and prosperous India. Disappointment due to no discussion on new pay scale Satyashankar Mishra, provincial president of the Government Teachers' Association, says that there has been great disappointment regarding Budget 2026. It was hoped that this time the government would definitely pay attention to teachers and the education system in the budget, but by showing a 7% increase, a rattle has been handed over (implying a trivial gesture). Along with increasing the budget, mismanagement was to be removed, which did not happen; money is merely being wasted, neither administrative management is correct nor financial management is correct. Ever since digitalization came, there has been a race among people to make everyone an engineer, everyone a doctor. No one talks about character education. Another problem has arisen in schools: with the aim of making education employment-oriented, they have paid a lot of attention to skill development in schools, but no attention is paid to the arrangement of teachers or their regular curriculum. Posts for important subjects are vacant, and even the teachers who are there have been given other tasks by the department. The condition of schools is very pathetic. First, their infrastructure should be improved, and teachers should be provided so that students can receive basic education. Teaching and learning inside schools should not be disturbed. These practices must be stopped. No one even discusses moral education; everyone wants to make them scientists. It would be better if cultural activities were promoted. Good students should be prepared so that a good society can be formed. The eighth pay commission has not even been discussed; all teaching staff are disappointed.

stories.title: UP PWD’s condemned vehicles 'ran' on paper:Rusted wheels, broken steering; officials siphoned millions in fake diesel claims
stories.summary: A 43-year-old UP PWD jeep, URE-3740, has been lying idle in the Lucknow PWD workshop for years. Its tires are rusted, seats torn, and the gearbox, steering, and dashboard are all broken. The interior is cluttered with old dustbins, posters, and spare tires. The department has officially declared it condemned. Yet, shockingly, officials continued to record it as “operational” on paper—claiming it covered over 5,000 km each month, enabling them to report ₹50,000 monthly in diesel expenses for a vehicle that doesn’t run. Investigations reveal this is not an isolated case—multiple condemned PWD vehicles are being misused in similar ways. What is this diesel expense scam involving condemned vehicles in the PWD? Which officers are responsible? To answer these questions, Dainik Bhaskar conducted a detailed investigation. To uncover and expose this malpractice, two types of case studies were conducted: Vehicles officially declared condemned but still recorded as running on paper. Vehicles not declared condemned yet lying unused for years, which are being “run” on paper to claim diesel expenses. Case Study- 1 The investigation team of Dainik Bhaskar documented that URE-3740 has been stationary in the PWD workshop for at least two years. Photos and videos confirmed the jeep is nothing more than scrap. The Chief Engineer, UK Singh, issued a letter on 26 August 2025, officially declaring the jeep condemned. He confirmed the order and stated a committee was formed to take action against those responsible, with the Senior Engineer RM Srivastava assigned to investigate. Despite this, a diesel bill from November 2025 showed 540 litres of diesel injected into the jeep over 16 days, amounting to Rs 49,816. Who benefited from the diesel scam? Responsibility for operating the jeep was assigned to Junior Engineer Technical (JET) Anil Verma. Verma claimed the jeep was parked from 1 January 2026, though he said it was operational until December 2025. He named drivers Sujit and Laddoo (Abhishek Bhardwaj) as having driven the jeep. Both drivers denied ever operating the jeep. Laddu refused to comment, while Sujeet stated he had no knowledge and threatened to file an FIR against the false allegations. Even the workshop employees confirmed the jeep had been parked for 2–3 years and never left the premises. The claims of December operations were therefore false. We called Laddu (Abhishek Bhardwaj). He said- I am a watchman, why would I drive a vehicle? He refused to say anything else besides this. Case study 2: Old ambassador misused Another case involved an old Ambassador car, UP32-BG-5326, lying in a scrapyard. Although not officially condemned, it too was falsely reported as operational to claim diesel expenses. A diesel bill from November 2025 showed ₹60,767 spent on this vehicle, signed off by Executive Engineer Ranjita Prasad. JET Anil Verma claimed the car was parked since December 2025, and its last actual use was by XEN Firdous Rahmani until October 2025. Both Rahmani and the driver, Saurabh Yadav, confirmed they had not used the car for months. How the scam operated At Alambagh Kohli Pump, diesel was supplied based on a PWD JE slip without verifying the vehicle number. The pump manager admitted: "We provided diesel as per the JE's signature. We did not check the vehicle number. For further details, you need to contact the pump owner." This shows a clear system-level lapse allowing officials to claim diesel for non-operational vehicles, funneling public funds into their pockets. Investigation findings Department Head says, ‘Action will be taken against offenders’ This investigation exposes a disturbing PWD practice: condemned vehicles are listed as running on paper to siphon diesel funds, highlighting corruption in government departments and lack of oversight.

stories.title: AKT University launches new visual gaming content degree programme:Vice chancellor says AI growth creates high-paying creative career; opportunities for students across Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Azad Technical University (AKTU) in Lucknow, which is affiliated to 765 colleges across Uttar Pradesh, will soon start a new course on AVGC (Audio Visual Gaming Content). The 18 credit course will be offered under the Minor Degree Programme. AKTU Vice Chancellor Prof JP Pandey shared this information in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar after the Union Budget. He said the growth of artificial intelligence has created many new career opportunities in this field. He added that the AVGC sector offers some of the highest salaries for young people globally and is becoming very popular among students because of its creative and interesting nature. Because of this, the launch of the course is being seen as very important. Read the special excerpts from the conversation Question: What has the technical education sector received in this budget? Answer: I would say this is a very good budget. It is technology-oriented. Almost all sectors have been covered in it. It can be called a step taken towards the goal of a developed India. This budget has been brought keeping in mind today's global circumstances, an attempt has been made to respond to the tariffs imposed by America. Question: What is special in the budget for those pursuing a career in technology and future students in this field? Answer: The Semiconductor 2.0 Mission launched by the government in this budget is very important. To increase research in the field of semiconductors and VLSI, a 'technical manpower' will have to be prepared. Experts will have to be trained to bring a boom in the electronics manufacturing sector. In such a situation, technical universities and technical institutions like ours will have to increase work on VLSI, semiconductor devices, and focus more on research. For this, everyone will have to make a concerted effort. Second, skilled manpower for AI will also have to be prepared. AI is to be used in every sector. For this, all faculty and teachers will have to be given AI training. Students will have to be trained in AI. Question: More than 750 technical institutions are affiliated with AKTU, what is important for those colleges? Answer: Besides semiconductor machines, we are also working in the direction of satellite and space technology. We are also working on the Quantum Mission. The goal is to make students of any degree course experts in new and on-demand courses through minor degrees. If the government talks about promoting the MSME or manufacturing sector, then the resource persons for that will come from us. Question: What changes have occurred since the implementation of NEP and how do you see the journey ahead? Answer: The biggest focus is on skill upgradation. The National Skill Qualification Framework has also been linked with the Core Care Ecosystem. All these things mentioned in the budget are also part of NEP. These are all a multidisciplinary approach. With this objective, minor degree programs are being started. The focus is on the all-round development of students. The initiative to set up content creator labs in 1500 schools and 500 colleges has also been taken in this budget. This can also be termed as a big step. Question: Which new course is AKTU going to start after this budget? Answer: We are going to start a minor degree course program related to AVGC, which stands for Audio Visual Content Creation. This will also be important from the students' perspective. Students are interested in this field. This is a very interesting field with new experiences. Students are also doing many innovations in gaming content and technology. With the advent of AI, this also has a lot of potential from an industry perspective. Thus, students are going to get many options and many new opportunities. We will plan and share this 18-credit course.

stories.title: Hail and rain alert in 27 UP districts today:Thunderstorm expected; weather likely to continue for 3 days, Muzaffarnagar records lowest temp in state
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh has changed suddenly. Rain accompanied by thunder, lightning and strong winds is continuing across western UP, adjoining Delhi-NCR, and Tarai regions bordering Uttarakhand. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a hailstorm warning for 27 districts today. In addition, 16 districts may experience gusty winds of 40–50 km per hour. Rainfall recorded in several Western UP districts Due to the impact of a western disturbance, rainfall that began in western UP continued intermittently throughout Sunday. In terms of temperature, Muzaffarnagar was the coldest place in the state, with the minimum temperature dropping to 6.4°C. Rainfall area to expand on Monday and Tuesday According to the Weather Department, the spread of rain will increase further on Monday and Tuesday. Central UP, the Awadh region, and parts of Bundelkhand are also likely to witness light to moderate rainfall with thunderstorms. Weather conditions are expected to remain similar for the next three days, till 4 February. What is causing the weather change? Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Singh explained the reason behind the ongoing weather activity. He said, Due to an active western disturbance over northern Pakistan, an induced cyclonic circulation has formed around southern Haryana. This system triggered rainfall in western UP. From late tonight to early morning, the rain may extend to central and adjoining eastern parts of the state. Additionally, the impact of two more western disturbances could keep the rainfall active till 4 February.

stories.title: MLA confronts minister, alleges officers are lying:Says roads are damaged and villages waterlogged; raises issue during proceedings in UP Assembly
stories.summary: BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput from Charkhari in Mahoba district of Uttar Pradesh is in the spotlight after he stopped state minister Swatantra Dev Singh on January 30. The MLA protested over the lack of drinking water in about 100 villages of his constituency and the poor condition of roads dug for pipeline work. He said people from nearly 90 percent of the district’s villages are questioning him, and he has no answers to give. Angry with his own government and officials, Brijbhushan Rajput told Dainik Bhaskar that the Namami Gange scheme, started to solve water problems in Bundelkhand, has still not been completed even after six years. He said village roads were dug in the name of the scheme and left unfinished, leading to waterlogging and serious problems for daily movement, while officers are showing figures that do not match the ground reality. Read the conversation with MLA Brijbhushan Rajput Question: Why was it necessary to block the minister's way on the road? Answer- We went to tell the minister that the 'Har Ghar Nal Yojana' (Tap Water to Every Home Scheme) running under Namami Gange in Bundelkhand is very important and multi-beneficial. The Prime Minister of the country gave this scheme understanding the pain of Bundelkhand. Because, even today, women here have to go miles away to fetch water. This major scheme to provide tap water to every house in every village of Bundelkhand has not been completed even after 6 years. Due to this scheme, the roads that were already built have been damaged. This has led to waterlogging in the villages. Villagers are facing great difficulty in commuting. Question: Are the MLAs not being heard? Answer: The work is not happening. We submitted letters. This issue was also raised in the assembly, but no concrete action was taken. When the minister came, we wanted to show him the ground reality. The officials are presenting false figures. 50 to 60 village heads also went with us. They wanted to tell the minister that the figures being presented from the stage are incorrect. The actual situation on the ground is completely different. Question: How many times have you complained to Minister Swatantra Dev Singh? Answer: Whenever the assembly session was in progress, I and other MLAs raised this issue in the house. However, no effective action has been taken so far. Question: Do the district officials not listen to you? Answer: I feel that the district officials have no interest in getting work done on this scheme. You can also go and see for yourself on the ground. The villagers are also showing the ground situation to the media and public representatives. There is no need to explain this separately. Question: Did you speak to the minister again after this incident? Answer: There was no conversation after this incident. He only said that the work would be done within 20 days. Now we have to see whether the work actually happens or not. Question: Did the Chief Minister, state president, or any senior leader speak to you? Answer: No, I did not try to speak to anyone. Question: How big is the Jal Jeevan Mission scam? Answer: I only want to say that there has been corruption in this scheme. This issue is directly related to the common people. Its truth should come before the government and the public. The MLA stands with the public. Read the full story On January 30, BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput clashed with Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh. The minister was returning from an event around 3:30 PM. That's when the MLA, along with 100 village heads, blocked his way. 30 cars and 20 bikes were parked in front of the minister's convoy. The Charkhari MLA had expressed displeasure to the minister over the lack of water supply in 100 villages of his constituency and the non-repair of roads dug for pipelines. MLA had told the minister - officers don't listen to us Seeing MLA Brijbhushan's displeasure, the minister made him sit in his car. Even then, the MLA kept hitting his hands together, telling the minister that all the village heads who have come to me have problems in their villages. There has been rampant negligence in the Har Ghar Nal Yojana (Tap Water to Every Home Scheme). You people don't see anything. The ground-level problem is very big. The MLA had also accused the scheme of corruption. He had said that officers don't listen to us. After the meeting with the minister, the MLA had said that the minister has given the officers 20 days to resolve the problems. Now, in 20 days, we will see how much the officers heed the minister's words. In the coming days, whoever needs to be stopped, we will stop them. Whatever fight I have to fight, I will not back down. Who is Brijbhushan Rajput? BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput from Charkhari (Mahoba) was born on May 28, 1982, in Orai (Jalaun). His father, Ganga Charan Rajput, has been a Lok Sabha MP 3 times (1989, 1996, 1998) and a Rajya Sabha MP (2009). Brijbhushan Rajput was married to Kanak Lodhi on May 9, 2005. They have two sons. Brijbhushan Rajput has inherited political conflict. His father, Ganga Charan Rajput, was known for controversies and defections in UP politics. Ganga Charan Rajput has been with Janata Dal, BJP, Congress, and BSP. He led many movements on electricity, water, and OBC issues in Bundelkhand. On May 18, 2004, after the UPA's victory, when there was talk of Sonia Gandhi becoming Prime Minister and she declined the post, a high-voltage drama unfolded outside the Congress office in Delhi. Ganga Charan Rajput climbed onto the roof of a car, brandished a pistol, and, pointing it at his own temple, threatened to shoot himself if Sonia Gandhi did not become PM. Today, a glimpse of that same political temperament is visible in his son, Brijbhushan Rajput. His message is clear: if work is not done, there will be trouble.

stories.title: Woman quits government job to build moringa enterprise:Lucknow’s Kamini builds 8,000-women network; cites Narendra Modi’s moringa paratha remark
stories.summary: While thousands of young Indians chase the security of government jobs, one woman chose to walk away from it — and built a model of entrepreneurship that today empowers more than a thousand women. Eight years ago, Dr Kamini Singh resigned from her prestigious government position to choose an uncertain but self-defined path. What followed was the creation of a unique “moringa army” — a network of nearly 1,000 women farmers — and a business that now records an annual turnover of ₹2.5 crore. Her success reached the national stage in October 2025, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited her for a meeting. During the interaction, the Prime Minister mentioned that he eats moringa (sahjan) parathas twice a week. The remark sparked widespread curiosity, leading to a surge in online searches about moringa’s nutritional benefits. This is the story of Dr Kamini Singh from Lucknow, who today manufactures more than 18 value-added products from moringa. Bhaskar spoke to Dr Kamini to understand why she left her government job, how she chose organic farming, and how moringa became the centre of her mission. Connecting women farmers through moringa Dr Kamini Singh brought together more than 1,000 women farmers through a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) and motivated them to cultivate moringa. She did not stop at farming alone. By focusing on value addition, she helped these women enter the market with finished products rather than raw produce. Today, most of the workforce associated with her enterprise consists of women. From cultivation to processing and packaging, women manage every stage of production on their own. At the unit, women can be seen cleaning and drying moringa and tulsi. Tulsi seeds and leaves are prepared for herbal green tea, while moringa leaves are processed for powder and other products. ‘Working here has made us financially strong’ Women associated with Dr Kamini’s company, Dr Moringa, say the work has strengthened them economically. Vindheshwari, one of the workers, says the products are not only beneficial for health but the employment has improved their financial condition. “Working here has given us regular income and confidence,” she says. More than 18 products from moringa According to Dr Kamini, women currently produce over 18 moringa-based products. These include moringa powder, tablets, moringa tea, handmade soap, moringa seed oil, biscuits, laddus and moringa pain oil. The products are sold in local markets as well as on online platforms and are witnessing strong demand. Who is Dr Kamini Singh? Dr Kamini Singh spent her childhood in the lanes of Varanasi before moving to Lucknow. She earlier worked as a senior researcher at the Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH). She told Bhaskar that she spent nearly seven years in government service. In 2015, she resigned, and in 2017 began her independent work. That was when she started developing the moringa project along with farmers. Why moringa? Dr Kamini explains that moringa (sahjan) is easy to cultivate and grows in most regions. Despite this, awareness about its benefits remains limited. “Moringa does not require chemical inputs. It gives good yields at low cost,” she says. This made it ideal for organic farming. Convincing farmers initially was difficult, but as they understood its benefits, more people joined the initiative. Over time, both production and farmers’ incomes increased. Struggles before success Success did not come easily. In 2018, Dr Kamini leased seven acres of land in Sidhauli, near Lucknow, and began moringa cultivation. Initially, there were no buyers. She then took a loan of ₹9 lakh to set up a processing unit. By drying moringa leaves, she began making powder, followed by soaps, capsules and other products. Gradually, the market expanded. Today, her annual turnover has crossed ₹2.5 crore. PM Modi and moringa paratha In September 2020, during the first anniversary of the Fit India Movement, Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke about his fondness for moringa parathas, which he eats twice a week. Moringa leaves, roots and fruits are rich in nutrients and vitamins, and are studied for their role in antioxidants, reducing inflammation, diabetes control and cancer research. Dr Kamini translated this nutritional potential into a ground-level organic agricultural model by connecting farmers directly to production and markets. Products beyond moringa Apart from moringa, products are also made from lemongrass and tulsi. Herbal teas prepared from tulsi seeds and leaves have strong market demand, while lemongrass products are known to support immunity. Where are the products available? Dr Kamini says moringa products are available at various retail outlets and can also be purchased through Amazon, Flipkart and the company’s official website. Prices range from ₹75 to ₹1,000, making them accessible to a wide section of consumers. Awareness stalls are also set up to educate people about moringa’s benefits. Farmers’ income up by 40% According to Dr Kamini, farmers’ income has increased by around 40% through moringa cultivation. Currently, more than 500 women are associated with Dr Moringa. Over 30 women are employed on a salaried basis, while others work on commission or daily wages. A cooperative and commercial model Dr Kamini follows both cooperative and commercial models. Women farmers cultivate moringa through the FPO network, while products are sold in the market. A significant portion of the profits is routed back to increase farmers’ incomes. About 30% of sales come from online platforms and 70% from offline channels, including local shops, Ayurvedic stores, medical outlets, agricultural fairs, exhibitions and FPO networks. Women also sell products directly in their local areas, strengthening employment and income at the grassroots. By turning moringa into a sustainable livelihood model, Dr Kamini Singh has not only built her own identity but has also shown how agriculture, entrepreneurship and women’s empowerment can grow together.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:NCP leaders meet Devendra Fadnavis; Avimukteshwarananda demands Yogi prove Hindu identity in 40 days more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. NCP leaders meet Devendra Fadnavis After the demise of Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar, discussions have intensified over giving his post to his wife, a possible merger of the two NCP factions, and the redistribution of key portfolios. Amid these demands, an NCP leader met Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis at his official residence, Varsha Bungalow. 2. Avimukteshwarananda demands Yogi prove Hindu identity in 40 days; Says, 'Declare cow as Gaumata' The dispute between Prayagraj Magh Mela administration and Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand continues. At a Varanasi press conference, he said that today, demanding cow protection and a ban on cow slaughter is treated as a major crime. 3. Prayagraj administration to apologise to Avimukteshwaranand The Prayagraj administration has reportedly agreed to apologize to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, according to his media representative Yogiraj Sarkar. This follows the Shankaracharya abruptly leaving the Magh Mela before the full moon bathing ceremony on February 1, shocking officials. 4. SC mandates free sanitary pads distribution, separate toilets in schools The Supreme Court directed all private and government schools in the country to provide free sanitary pads to girls. Schools must have separate washrooms for boys and girls. Schools failing to comply will have their recognition revoked. 5. BJP’s regional balance breaks down in UP The UP BJP’s government and organisational balance is disrupted, with Kashi and Gorakhpur regions dominating key posts, while Awadh and western regions lag. Political analysts warn that this imbalance could affect Assembly elections if not corrected. 6. Kanpur road built in 24 hours breaks immediately A 400-meter road in Jhandapur village, Ghatampur tehsil, Kanpur, built in just 24 hours, became unusable the next day. Gravel loosened under bicycles, and potholes appeared under pedestrian steps, raising allegations of a scam. 7. Trump claims Putin halted attack on Ukraine at his request US President Donald Trump said on Thursday at the White House that he personally requested Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt attacks on the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, for one week due to extreme winter conditions. 8. Transgender skin therapist performs spiritual penance at Magh Mela Priyanshi Das, a transgender skin therapist from Prayagraj, shared her life story at the Magh Mela. She realized at age 7-8 that her body didn’t match her female identity, despite being born male, and expressed her love for dressing as a girl. 9. Girls escape shelter home in Mathura to meet boyfriends; scale 35-foot wall using dupatta Five girls escaped a women’s shelter in Mathura on January 26, climbing to the rooftop and using twisted dupattas and blankets as a rope to scale a 35-feet-high wall, evading CCTV. All were later traced and returned to the shelter home. 10. Bangladesh cancels land allotment for Indian SEZ Bangladesh has cancelled the land allotment for a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Chittagong that was earlier given to India. The Yunus-led government has now handed over the land to China to set up a drone manufacturing facility.

stories.title: ‘If I speak, there will be riots,’ says Dhirendra Shastri:Targets Muslims over triple talaq and religious customs
stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham’s head priest, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri said that India would not become a Hindu nation by abusing Muslims, but by reforming shortcomings within the Hindu community itself. Speaking in Banda, he said Hindus must correct their own malpractices, only then can the country move forward. Referring to divorce practices, Shastri said that in some communities divorce is frequent, while in the Hindu community it involves lengthy legal procedures. “Wherever you look, there is divorce. May God protect us. We have nothing to say, otherwise riots may break out,” he remarked. He added that different communities have their own systems and ways of life, and there is nothing wrong with that. “If we stay within limits, it will benefit everyone,” he said. Shastri further stated, “Our job is to go from door to door, their job is to create obstacles, and God’s job is to take care of everything. Remember one thing—if you have faith in God, He will never let your faith break.” ‘India will not become a Hindu nation by abusing Muslims: Shastri He also cautioned against mixing religious practices, saying that people should have complete faith in one path rather than switching between different rituals and then blaming God for unanswered prayers. Pandit Dhirendra Shastri visited Banda on the invitation of BJP MLA Prakash Dwivedi. After arriving, his convoy reached the MLA’s residence in Khurand. From there, he offered prayers along with the MLA at the Kailasheshwar Mahadev temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and participated in the ongoing Sundarkand recitation at the temple. See pictures of the temple More than 8,000 devotees reached the temple after learning about Dhirendra Shastri’s visit. He is scheduled to hold a saintly court at the legislator’s residence. This marks Dhirendra Shastri’s second visit to Banda within a span of 10 days. Earlier, he had narrated the Hanumant Katha from January 16 to 20, during which a divine court was also organised. Over one lakh devotees attended the five-day religious event. 5-day Hanumant Katha held in Banda Pandit Dhirendra Shastri narrated the Hanumant Katha in Banda from January 16 to 20. Several prominent leaders and religious figures attended the event, including Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’, Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh, former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, and Mahant Rajudas of Ayodhya’s Hanumangarhi. In the story, Dhirendra Shastri had also sung, "Keep pushing and shoving in the court, eat from the rich. A day will come when you yourself will become rich. Some will become rich quickly, some slowly, but our Balaji's devotee will one day become a wealthy person." He said, “The fair that was held in Banda was no less than any Mahakumbh. Such blessings of Bajrangbali showered that this event will be recorded in Bundelkhand's history for centuries. Devotees can be seen everywhere. People are walking up to 5-5 kilometers for darshan,”.

stories.title: Anupam Kher visits Kashi:Actor offers prayers at Baba Vishwanath and Sankat Mochan Temple, shares 'I found peace here'
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Anupam Kher recently embarked on a spiritual journey to Kashi, immersing himself in the city's sacred atmosphere. He began his visit at the revered Baba Vishwanath Temple, where he offered prayers and performed darshan, chanting "Har Har Mahadev" with devotion. Accompanied by astrologer Chandramauli, the actor sought the blessings of Lord Bholenath, reciting Shiva mantras with heartfelt reverence. "My heart is filled with joy upon visiting Kashi," Anupam Kher expressed, reflecting the profound impact of the experience. Following his visit to Baba Vishwanath, Kher proceeded to the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple, where he offered prayers to Bajrangbali. He prayed for the prosperity, peace, and happiness of both the nation and his family. Throughout his temple visits, Kher engaged in worship with deep devotion, spending time in meditation and reflection. His spiritual sojourn to Kashi underscored his deep faith and connection to India's rich cultural heritage. "Darshan of Lord Hanuman brings inner peace' Anupam Kher further stated, "Coming to Kashi, he feels spiritual peace. Visiting Baba Vishwanath and Sankat Mochan Hanuman ji brings special solace to the mind. In today's time, positive energy, peace, and unity are most needed for the country and society, and with this sentiment, he has prayed. Enthusiasm among devotees to see Anupam Kher As soon as the news of Anupam Kher's arrival in Kashi was received, enthusiasm was also seen among the devotees present in the temple premises. Many people took pictures with him and greeted him. The actor also accepted everyone's greetings and praised the spiritual glory of Kashi. Will participate in Banaras Lit Fest Actor Anupam Kher will also participate in the Banaras Lit Fest starting today. More than 200 speakers, artists, writers, and performers, along with people from 50 countries, will participate in the three-day event held from January 30, 2026, to February 1.

stories.title: BJP MLA stops minister’s convoy in Mahoba, sparks clash:Heated exchange between Swatantra Dev and Brijbhushan Rajput over complaint
stories.summary: In Mahoba, BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput stopped the convoy of Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh. He, along with 100 village heads, stopped the minister's convoy by parking vehicles in the middle of the road while returning from the Yuva Udghosh program. The MLA expressed displeasure over the dilapidated condition of roads in his assembly constituency. He said that villagers are facing problems due to roads dug under the Jal Jeevan Mission. ‘What answer should I give for this?’ he asked. During this, the MLA's supporters clashed with the CO Sadar and Kotwal. Swatantra Dev Singh said, I am ready to visit 40 villages. It is our job to provide water. Officers are with me. If roads are dug somewhere and water is not available, I will suspend the officers. There was a heated clash between workers and security personnel with the CO Sadar and Kotwal. The entire incident took place near Ramshree Mahavidyalaya in Mahoba. 3 photos related to the incident

stories.title: Yogi govt raises ministers’ financial approval limit to ₹50 cr:Anganwadi workers to get salaries on fixed dates
stories.summary: The UP government has enhanced the financial powers of ministers, allowing them to approve projects worth up to Rs 50 crore, up from the earlier limit of Rs 10 crore. Projects costing up to Rs 150 crore will now be approved by the Finance Minister, while proposals above this amount will require the Chief Minister’s approval. In another major relief, Anganwadi workers will now receive their honorarium on a fixed date every month. The state government will ensure timely payment from its own budget without waiting for the Centre’s share, ending delays in salaries. CM Yogi conducted a high-level review of the finance department on Friday. Major decisions were taken to further accelerate the pace of development in UP. Read the main points 1- No delay in annual plan CM has given an ultimatum to all departments. He said - get your Annual Action Plan approved by April 15 at all costs. The department that shows negligence, its report will be sent directly to the CM Office. If the cost of any project increases by more than 15 percent, then re-approval will have to be taken by stating the reason. 2- Fixed maintenance system now in government buildings too CM Yogi said that like roads, a 5-year maintenance system will now be mandatory in the construction of new government buildings. This condition will be included in the contract. There is a need to create a separate corpus fund for the maintenance of old government buildings. 3- UP ranks number one in capital expenditure in country It was informed in the meeting that in the financial year 2023-24, Uttar Pradesh incurred capital expenditure of more than Rs 1.10 lakh crore, which is the highest in the country. The state spent more on development works than it borrowed. 9.39 percent of the total budget was spent on investment. In NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index, UP has risen from 37 points in 2014 to 45.9 in 2023 and is at the top in the front-runner category. According to the RBI report, UP ranks second in the country with 11.6 percent in terms of its tax revenue. 4- Third-party audit mandatory in construction Facilities like the online budget module, cyber treasury, paperless bills, and GPF slips on DigiLocker have been implemented in the finance department. By April 2026, the treasury will become completely paperless. For the quality of construction works, third-party audits will be conducted by institutions like IIT and NIT. CM Yogi Adityanath said, Uttar Pradesh has set a new record in financial discipline. Now the goal is to make the state the country's strongest financial administration state through quality, transparency, and digital systems. The process needs to be made fast, simple, and completely transparent. If approvals are received on time, work will also be completed on time.

stories.title: Saudi-bound aircraft makes emergency landing in Mumbai:Flight returned nearly 100 minutes after takeoff from Lucknow
stories.summary: A Saudia Airlines flight heading to Saudi Arabia from Lucknow airport was forced to make an emergency landing on Friday after developing a technical snag shortly after take-off. According to sources, the aircraft faced a cabin pressure issue when it was near Mumbai, causing breathing difficulties for some passengers. Given the situation, the pilot first contacted Mumbai airport seeking permission to land, but clearance was not granted. The pilot then reached out to Lucknow airport. After receiving permission for an emergency landing, the aircraft turned back and safely landed in Lucknow around 82 minutes later. Once the fault was rectified, the flight resumed its journey to Jeddah. The aircraft was operating as Saudia Airlines flight SV-891 and was carrying 275 passengers, along with four pilots and six crew members. Technical fault rectified According to information, the aircraft was scheduled to depart at 12:05 pm but could take off only at 12:23 pm. Around 1:45 pm, the flight was forced to return mid-air due to the technical issue. Passengers were not deboarded during the halt. Engineers later rectified the fault, after which the aircraft departed for Jeddah at 4:20 pm. What is cabin pressure? Cabin pressure is an artificial air-pressure system maintained inside an aircraft. It ensures that passengers do not face breathing difficulties even when the plane is flying at an altitude of 30,000 to 40,000 feet. The system maintains air pressure equivalent to an altitude of around 6,000 to 8,000 feet, allowing passengers to breathe comfortably throughout the flight. Earlier incident involving the same airline Earlier, on July 15, 2025, a Saudia Airlines aircraft developed a fault during landing at Lucknow airport. Sparks were seen coming from near the wheels as the plane landed. During the landing of flight SV-3112, sparks and smoke were observed from the wheels, prompting the pilot to immediately stop the aircraft and alert air traffic control. At the time, 242 Haj pilgrims were onboard the flight. Smoke seen immediately after landing on runway Sources said that as the aircraft landed on the runway after the pilot deployed the landing gear, a fault developed in the left-side wheel. The malfunction is believed to have been caused by a sudden leak in the hydraulic system. This led to heavy smoke and sparks, creating panic-like conditions at the airport. Sources added that had this fault occurred during take-off, it could have resulted in a major accident. It was further informed that during the return of Haj pilgrims, Saudia Airlines aircraft operate flights from Jeddah carrying pilgrims to Lucknow. However, the aircraft usually returns empty from Lucknow without carrying passengers back.

stories.summary: The ancestral practice known as Khoni or Paathara was once observed by farmers along the banks of the Mahendratanaya River. Several factors—including lack of space and awareness, as well as changes in rural architecture—have contributed to its decline. This tradition thrived in the inland, hilly terrain, where underground grain storage was effective. Over time, however, this ancient practice has gradually faded, becoming more of a story from the past, writes T. Appala Naidu.

stories.title: Terror suspect prepares hit list targeting Delhi, UP:Buys weapons for killings; accused of remarks against Islam and Prophet during interrogation by police
stories.summary: Gujarat Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) arrested a suspicious youth from the Charpul area of Navsari on January 25, 2026. The accused has been identified as Faizan Sheikh, a resident of Rampur in Uttar Pradesh. According to ATS, Faizan had prepared a list of people who made statements against Islam and the Prophet and was planning to kill them. The agency has recovered a list containing seven names from his possession. The accused had prepared a list of people from Delhi-UP ATS investigation revealed that Faizan Sheikh was influenced by the radical ideology of banned terrorist organizations Jaish-e-Mohammed and Al-Qaeda. Interrogation of Faizan revealed that he was collecting data of those who made statements against the Prophet. He had originally prepared a list of people from Delhi and Uttar Pradesh. He had also bought a revolver with the money earned from tailoring clothes for murder. However, the accused has not attacked anyone yet. Faizan had made a list of these seven names 29 pages written in Urdu and Arabic also recovered Faizan was in contact with members of terrorist organizations like Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba and had confessed that he was ready to carry out any incident at their behest. However, ATS apprehended him before he could execute his intention. 29 pages written in Urdu and Arabic were also recovered from him, which are being investigated. Had been working as a tailor in Navsari for some years The accused is originally from Rampur district of Uttar Pradesh. For the past few years, he had been earning his livelihood by working as a tailor in Navsari, Gujarat. Large-scale order-based work is done here, and artisans from Uttar Pradesh work.

stories.title: Avimukteshwarananda demands Yogi prove his Hindu identity in 40 days:Says, 'Declare cow as Gaumata, or the saffron robe is just for show'
stories.summary: The dispute between the Prayagraj Magh Mela administration and Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand is continuing. Meanwhile, the Shankaracharya held a press conference in Varanasi. He said that in today’s time, demanding protection of cows and a ban on cow slaughter has become the biggest crime. He said that whenever anyone raised their voice against cow slaughter, governments tried to suppress it. He alleged that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and his associate Rambhadracharya are currently surrounding and attacking those who demand a ban on cow slaughter in different ways. The Shankaracharya said that he was even asked to show proof of being a Shankaracharya, whereas religion does not depend on any certificate. He alleged that attempts are being made to damage his image within the Sanatani community and that people connected to those in power are behind this. He said that when he was asked for a certificate, he provided it, but now the Chief Minister should give proof of being a Hindu. According to him, being a Hindu is not limited to speeches or clothing, but is linked to cow service and protection of religion. What has happened so far On January 18, while Avimukteshwaranand was going for a ritual bath at the Magh Mela, police stopped his palanquin. When his followers protested, there was pushing and shoving. Allegations were made that disciples were dragged by their hair. After this, the Shankaracharya sat on a protest outside his camp and did not enter it for 11 days. The administration issued two notices within two days, asking for proof of him being a Shankaracharya. Avimukteshwaranand replied to both notices. Chief Minister Yogi, without taking any name, referred to “Kalanemi”, which further deepened the dispute. In response, Avimukteshwaranand compared Yogi to Kalanemi and Aurangzeb. The saint community became divided into two groups over the issue, while all three Shankaracharyas supported Avimukteshwaranand. The Shankaracharya demanded that the administration apologise, only then would he take the holy bath. In his support, Bareilly City Magistrate resigned on January 26. After 24 hours, Ayodhya Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar resigned in support of the Chief Minister. On the morning of January 28, the Shankaracharya left the Magh Mela. This sudden development surprised everyone. He said that his heart was deeply hurt, and that he was leaving without taking the holy dip.

stories.title: Students dance in burqa at Gonda Republic Day program:College management apologizes costume selection, DIOS orders investigation
stories.summary: At a college Republic Day program in Gonda, female students were seen dancing on stage wearing burqas, triggering widespread outrage after a video of the incident surfaced. Reports claim that in the video, more than six Hindu students perform Bollywood songs while dressed in burqas. The video originates from Guru Charan Srivastava AR Inter College. Following protests by local residents at the college, the management issued a written apology on social media. The college clarified that a dance performance was intended on a horror-themed song, but the costumes were mistakenly selected. They also stated that the background music had been edited on social media, presenting the performance in a misleading manner. DIOS orders investigation, principal and manager summoned The District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) has ordered a formal investigation into the matter. The college principal and manager have been summoned for questioning. The incident took place in Nirmal Nagar Ballipur, under the Manakapur police station area, approximately 35 kilometers from the district headquarters. Dainik Bhaskar has not independently verified the viral videos. Community outrage and social media response The video has provoked anger among both Hindu and Muslim communities. Social media users have described the act as offensive to religious sentiments. Questions have been raised about the school administration’s oversight, and many have demanded strict action against the responsible individuals. Critics have warned that if such incidents occur in schools, it undermines the institution’s credibility. Multiple organizations have expressed objections to the video online. College management issues apology Seeing the controversy escalate, college manager Raju Srivastava issued a written apology. While submitting the apology at Manakapur police station, he stated that during the Republic Day program, students performed a “ghost team” mixed song as part of the cultural event. He expressed regret if anyone’s sentiments were hurt and apologized on behalf of the school family. The manager also confirmed that no such program would be organized in the future. DIOS orders full investigation Taking the viral video seriously, DIOS Dr. Ramchandra has directed a comprehensive investigation. Further actions will be based on the findings. Both the college principal and manager have been summoned for questioning. Investigation ordered, college manager and principal summoned DIOS Dr. Ramchandra said- The viral video has come to our attention, in which some female students are seen dancing while wearing burqas. This video is said to be from Republic Day. The college management and principal have been summoned. I am personally investigating the entire matter. Action will be taken based on whatever facts come to light in the investigation.

stories.title: Greater Noida female influencer faces 27 km chase by youths:Calls husband as men continue making obscene gestures while she drives home
stories.summary: A case has emerged in Greater Noida involving a well-known female social media influencer being chased by car-riding youths. It is alleged that from Delhi’s DND Flyover to Pari Chowk in Greater Noida, the youths followed her for nearly 27 kilometers. They repeatedly tried to overtake her. Hanging out of the moving car windows, the youths made obscene gestures. The chase continued until the woman reached her home. Frightened, she stopped her car and called her husband to inform him about the incident. During this time, the accused were also standing near the scene. Since she was close to home, her husband arrived at the spot quickly. He contacted the police and provided complete details of the incident. Until the police reached the location, arguments continued between the accused and the woman’s husband. Meanwhile, officers from the Knowledge Park police station arrived and spoke to both parties. However, the woman refused to file a formal complaint, so the police advised the accused and released them. The husband later shared a video of the incident on social media. The woman has 5.7 million followers on Instagram, while her husband has over 2 million followers. The woman was returning home in a BMW, and the youths blocked her car from the front at multiple points. Police had intended to arrest and send the accused to jail, but the woman and her husband, identified as Lakhan and Neetu, refused. Incident in Sequence January 27: Returning Home in a BMW The woman’s husband said that on January 27, his wife was returning from Delhi to their home in Greater Noida in a BMW. Near the DND Flyover, some youths riding in another car began following her vehicle. On the way, they repeatedly tried to overtake her and made obscene gestures. The Woman Called Her Husband in Fear The husband added that when the youths continued following her near Pari Chowk, she became extremely frightened. Panicked, she called him and explained the entire incident. At that time, their home was approximately 15 minutes away. Upon receiving the information, he immediately rushed to the location and informed the police. The Knowledge Park police station subsequently arrived at the scene. Police Warn Accused and Release Them According to the husband, the police spoke to both parties. Arrangements were being made to send the accused to jail, but the woman refused to lodge a complaint. Following this, the police issued warnings to the accused and released them.

stories.title: Prayagraj administration to apologize to Avimukteshwaranand:Shankaracharya sets 2 conditions, while 2 senior Lucknow officials to ensure respected Sangam Snan ceremony
stories.summary: The Prayagraj administration has reportedly agreed to apologize to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, according to the spiritual leader’s media representative Yogiraj Sarkar. The announcement comes after Shankaracharya abruptly left the Magh Mela for Varanasi, shocking officials who had expected him to stay until the Mela’s full moon bathing ceremony on February 1. Two senior officials from Lucknow contacted Shankaracharya after his arrival in Varanasi, promising him a respected Sangam bath on the Mela’s Purnima day. The Shankaracharya set two conditions for the administration: Officials from the state will accompany Shankaracharya back to Prayagraj for the ceremonial bath. High-level meeting on January 27: Points of disagreement The conflict between Shankaracharya and the administration lasted 11 days, beginning with the Mauni Amavasya bathing incident. On January 27 evening, a secret high-level meeting was held at the Dharm Sangh camp near Shankaracharya’s tent. Present at the meeting were Rishi Raj and Deputy Mela Officer Dayanand Prasad, along with other Mela officials. Representing Shankaracharya was Mahant Shridharanand Brahmachari from Mankameshwar Temple. Shankaracharya’s disciples did not attend the meeting. Three points were agreed upon by both sides: However, two key issues remained unresolved: Mahant Shridharanand insisted that without a written apology, Shankaracharya would not accept their apology. In 2 pictures, see the scenes of Shankaracharya leaving the Magh Mela and the ashram being removed- Incident timeline and Background Shankaracharya explains decision to leave Mela Before leaving, Shankaracharya addressed the media, saying: I am deeply saddened to leave without taking the bath. I came here with faith and devotion, but an incident occurred that I never expected. Those who insulted Sanatan traditions must be held accountable. He rejected a proposal from the administration to hold the Sangam bath, stating that anger and hurt prevent peace, even in holy waters. Yogiraj Sarkar added that Shankaracharya’s decision was also influenced by the assault on his disciples during Mauni Amavasya.

stories.title: SP MP is protecting Moid Khan:Ayodhya rape victim’s mother alleges DNA report was manipulated, fears for her safety, and will approach the High Court
stories.summary: "Samajwadi Party MP Moid Khan is being protected, I think even the test report has been altered. How can we forget what happened to my daughter?" mother of the rape victim A daughter was raped on July 29, 2024. Samajwadi Party leader Moid Khan and his servant Raju Khan were accused in the case. POCSO Court Judge Nirupama Vikram has acquitted Moid Khan. His servant Raju Khan was found guilty and sentenced to 20 years in prison. Moid Khan will remain in jail for now because a separate case under the Gangster Act is also registered against him. The victim’s family is still in deep pain, say reports. Read the report The Bhaskar team reached the home of the rape victim living in the Bhadarsa area of Ayodhya. There was silence at the gate, and CCTVs were installed on the front pillar. Their light was drawing attention. Inside the house, the rape victim, her mother, and brother were found. The mother spoke to us with a heavy heart. Read the full conversation Question: Was the advocacy on your behalf not done properly? Answer: Everyone knows Moid Khan did wrong. I don't know how the court is letting him go. We are not educated, so advocacy could not be done on our behalf. The police did not investigate properly, otherwise, Moid would not have been released. This is not right, our hearing was not done properly. Question: Raju Khan was sentenced to 20 years in prison and a fine of 50 thousand? Answer: He (Raju) should not get 20 years in prison, he should be hanged. He has ruined my daughter's life, his house should also be demolished. Now we will go to the High Court. Question: Will you be in danger if Moid Khan is released? Answer: Even when these people were in jail, we were scared. Now that we've heard Moid Khan is being released, the danger has increased. Ever since my daughter was raped, we have stayed inside the house, but for how long will we stay. Now it will be difficult to go out. We demand security, the police used to come before, but now no one comes. There are 2 CCTV cameras installed outside our house, which were installed by the police, and we monitor with them. Question: Has Moid Khan received a clean chit in the DNA report? Answer: We are not satisfied with the DNA test. Something went wrong. These MPs are protecting Moeed Khan, which is why our hearing is not happening. The test report has been altered, how can we forget what happened to my daughter. Raju's DNA also matched On July 29, 2024, a 12-year-old girl filed a gangrape case in the Bhadarsa area of Ayodhya. The girl was pregnant at that time. Moeed Khan and his servant Raju Khan were named as accused in this. Moeed and Raju were arrested the next day after the FIR was registered. Later, on August 7, 2024, the minor rape survivor's abortion was performed at Queen Mary's Hospital in Lucknow, following a court order. The victim alleged that she worked with Raju Khan, and about two and a half months ago, Raju had introduced her to Moeed. In the complaint filed at the police station, she claimed that Moeed, along with his servant, raped her. They recorded a video of this incident. Using the video to intimidate and threaten her, Moeed and Raju continued to sexually exploit her for about two and a half months. Now, Moeed has been proven innocent in court, while his servant Raju has been found involved in the incident by the court. Raju's DNA also matched the DNA of the fetus. UP government had run a bulldozer After this incident, the administration had demolished Moid's bakery and shopping mall. At that time, the then District Magistrate of Ayodhya, Chandra Vijay Singh, had said - Moid Khan's bakery was illegally built on pond land, which is why action was taken. CM Yogi, while giving a statement in the assembly, claimed Moied Khan's association with the SP. He had said - Moied in Ayodhya, who is a leader of the Samajwadi Party and a member of the MP's team in Ayodhya, has been found involved in the rape of a 12-year-old minor girl. The Chief Minister had also met the family of the rape victim after the case was registered. Following this, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had demanded DNA tests for Moied and Raju. Moeed got an advantage on 4 points in court Advocate Saeed Khan, who defended Moeed, told a media channel that the results of the DNA test were most crucial in this decision. The court considered Moeed innocent and 'honorably acquitted' him. 1. A DNA test of the fetus was conducted on the court's order, which did not match Moeed's DNA. 2. The prosecution could not even prove where the incident took place. The prosecution presented a total of 13 witnesses in support of the rape victim. 3. It was also claimed that a video was made during the incident, but no video was presented as evidence in court. 4. Contradictions have also emerged regarding the crime scene during the police investigation. During the police investigation, different claims were made about the incident occurring both under a tree outside the bakery and inside the bakery. Speaking to the media, Special Public Prosecutor Virendra Kumar said- This decision will be challenged in the High Court. We will continue to fight the case.

stories.title: Kanpur road built in just 24 hours:Susbstandard materials used, surface breaks under bicycles and pedestrians walking on the road
stories.summary: A scam has come to light in Jhandapur village, Ghatampur tehsil, Kanpur, over a 400-meter road that broke within a day. The road was built in just 24 hours, but villagers said it became unusable the next day. Gravel came loose even when the bicycle brakes were applied, and potholes appeared when villagers stepped on it. Villagers protested, but the contractor finished the work, packed the machines, and left. Now, they have filed a complaint on the Chief Minister’s portal and plan to approach the District Magistrate’s office. When a Bhaskar reporter visited the site, villagers showed the poor condition of the road. See 2 pictures- Contractors built the road and left in 24 hours Dainik Bhaskar's team reached Jhandapur village, about 55 kilometers from Kanpur. Abhay, Saurabh, Govind, Sumit, Sunil, Puneet, Manish, and Ravindra from the village showed us the reality of the road on the spot. According to the villagers, contractor Piyush Kushwaha started the work late at night and built the road within 24 hours. However, the construction, done by disregarding standards, is now crumbling in many places, and the road has caved in in several sections. Villagers said - Roller not used, material substandard Villagers allege that during road construction, neither proper filling was done nor was a road roller used. As a result, the road has sunk from the edges. The villagers say that substandard material was used; the situation is such that if a cyclist applies brakes, the road starts to crumble. Work done at night despite protests Villagers said that they had protested against the substandard construction, but the contractor did not listen to anyone. The work was completed overnight and the machines were removed. After the condition of the road came to light, officials were called to complain and the matter was also registered on the CM portal. District Panchayat member had raised questions earlier Rajnarayan Kuril, District Panchayat member from Patari, had recently written a letter to Kanpur DM Jitendra Pratap Singh, alleging a scam in a four hundred meter road. He had accused contractor Piyush Kushwaha of disregarding standards and manipulating measurements in the construction work. The DM had assured investigation and action. Claim of irregularities in works worth crores The District Panchayat member alleges that the concerned contractor's firm has carried out works worth 4 to 5 crore rupees for CC roads, asphalt roads, and paved roads in the District Panchayat area. Similar irregularities are suspected in all these works as well. He has demanded a high-level investigation into all the works. District Panchayat President remained silent On the question of the road scam and irregularities, District Panchayat President Swapnil Varun remained silent. When contacted, the call was disconnected, stating that he was in a meeting. Villagers demand - investigation, action against those responsible The villagers of Jhandapur say that if action is not taken in time, they will reach the DM office and protest. They clearly state - the road is paved on paper, but not on the ground. The scam should be investigated, and all those responsible should be acted upon.

stories.title: Dense fog returns in UP, rain alert for 3 days:Visibility drops to 10 meters, icy winds sweep through cities, leaving people shivering amid severe cold conditions
stories.summary: Dense fog envelops Uttar Pradesh today. Around 30 districts, including Lucknow, Jhansi, Agra and Aligarh, have remained under dense fog since Friday morning. In several districts such as Aligarh and Jhansi, visibility has dropped to as low as 10 metres. Strong icy winds have intensified the cold during morning and evening hours, while dew drops are being felt like light drizzling rain. Roads appeared largely deserted. People stepping out of vehicles complained of numbness in their hands. Those venturing out for essential work were seen wrapped in warm clothing. Bonfires were lit at several places along roadsides to combat the cold. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for the next three to four days, raising the possibility of another spell of severe cold. According to the Meteorological Department, a fresh western disturbance is becoming active over the state from February 1. Due to its impact, rainfall is likely in both western and eastern parts of Uttar Pradesh between February 1 and February 3. Senior scientist at Meteorological Center Lucknow, Atul Kumar Singh said - Minimum temperatures across the state may drop by 3 to 5 degrees in the next 24 hours. Light fog may persist in eastern and terai regions. Condition of major cities Lucknow: Light haze and fog prevailed in the morning. Icy winds made the cold more severe. The maximum temperature is expected to be around 21 degrees Celsius, while the minimum may hover near 10 degrees. On Thursday, the minimum temperature was recorded at 11.2 degrees Celsius. Jhansi: Dense fog prevailed in the morning, with visibility around 10 metres. The minimum temperature was recorded at 10 degrees Celsius. The Utkal Express travelling from Haridwar to Puri was delayed by 12 hours, while 15 other trains are also running behind schedule. Agra: Dense fog prevailed in the morning, accompanied by icy winds that increased the chill. Fog remained lighter within the city but denser in outer areas. The morning temperature was around 8 degrees Celsius. Dew drops felt like rain. The AQI was recorded at 266, falling in the moderate category. Aligarh: Dense fog prevailed in the morning with visibility around 10 metres. Cold winds intensified the chill. The maximum temperature was recorded at 19 degrees Celsius and the minimum at 8 degrees Celsius. How will the weather be for 3 days January 31: Fog likely in some districts, with winds blowing at speeds of 30–40 km per hour. February 1: Rain likely in many parts of eastern and western UP. February 2: Rain likely in many parts of eastern and western Uttar Pradesh, along with strong winds. January rainfall 39% below normal January remained dull in terms of rainfall this year. According to Meteorological Department data, Lucknow received 8.6 mm of rainfall in January, against a normal average of 14.1 mm. This marks a deficiency of nearly 39 percent. Impact of fog in UP; Know how fog forms Crops suffer heavy damage due to rain, wind and hail Agriculture expert Siddharth Singh said that if wheat crops lodge due to strong winds, grain weight reduces, potentially leading to a production loss of up to 20 percent. Sugarcane crops have also lodged extensively, raising concerns over cane damage and reduced yield. Mustard and vegetable crops have suffered significant damage due to rain. Excess waterlogging in fields has caused mustard pods to fall to the ground, increasing the risk of grain damage. Waterlogging has also led to rotting in vegetable crops. Farmers engaged in vegetable cultivation have suffered the maximum losses due to the recent weather conditions.
