stories.title: Girls escape 'captivity' to meet boyfriends:Made rope from dupatta in Mathura, scaled 35-feet wall hiding from CCTV; all traced and brought back in shelter home
stories.summary: Five girls made a daring escape from a women’s shelter home in Mathura, smartly picking January 26, when most staff members were exhausted after Republic Day duties. Around 10 PM, the girls climbed to the shelter’s rooftop and used dupattas and blankets to twist a makeshift rope, which they used to scale down the nearly 35-feet-high wall. Police traced and caught four of the girls within 24 hours from Delhi, Agra, Aligarh, and Mahavan, and brought them back to the shelter home. Meanwhile, the fifth girl, a resident of Nohzheel, was recovered from her home on January 28. During questioning, it was revealed that two girls from Delhi and Agra had fled to meet their boyfriends, against whom rape cases had already been registered. The other three girls were reportedly distressed by family issues and supported the plan, helping them execute the escape When the Agra girl called her boyfriend, he panicked and sent his girlfriend's location to the police through a lawyer. To find out how these girls escaped and made it back to the shelter home, Dainik Bhaskar visited the women's shelter home in Chaitanya Vihar. Read the ground report... Story of 2 girls who ran away to meet their boyfriends FIR of rape filed against boyfriend, expressed threat to life when found Chaitanya Vihar is among the posh areas of Vrindavan. The women's shelter home is built near the flyover here. All its arrangements are managed by the Women and Child Welfare Department. 8 months ago, the girls' protection home was also shifted to this campus. It houses POCSO Act victims and girls who are found after going missing from home. After discussions with officials, it came to light that currently 93 girls from Mathura, Vrindavan and nearby districts were staying in the shelter home. All the girls are between 14 to 17 years of age. In this shelter home, 2 girls from Agra and Delhi were also present. Their families had filed cases of kidnapping and rape against their boyfriends. The allegation was that the boys misled our daughters and kidnapped them. Then raped them. Actually, these girls were in love affairs. The girls had run away from home with their boyfriends. In the family, fathers and brothers had filed rape FIRs against the boyfriends to trap them. When the police recovered the girls, they refused to go with their families. Since they were minors, they had expressed fear for their lives. Therefore, they were kept in the shelter home. Stole key under pretense of helping staff Both girls from Agra and Delhi were brought to Mathura's shelter home. The love stories of both girls were similar. Both started living in the same common room. Meanwhile, they quickly became friends. Both shared their stories with each other. On January 20, the girls planned that they needed to escape from this confinement. They were worried about how their boyfriends and family members would be doing. They wanted to meet them. The girls first understood the structure of the entire shelter home building. They found no weak points. The walls were quite high. CCTV cameras were installed everywhere. The girls realized that after reaching the roof, there was no way out except jumping from a height of 35 feet. However, the gate leading to the stairs to the roof was kept locked. The girls understood that if they wanted to escape, they would need the key to this lock. They first stole the key to the stairway gate under the pretense of helping the shelter home staff with their work. After this, they waited for 1 day. Girls' plan leaked to 3 more girls The escape plan of the girls became known to 3 more girls living with them. Those three were brought to the shelter home in different POCSO Act cases. This way, by January 25, the number of girls planning to escape reached 5. All the girls planned together that January 26th would be the best day to escape. Because, officers and staff would remain busy throughout the day in Republic Day programs. At 10 PM when everyone had dinner and went to sleep, the girls came out of their respective rooms. After unlocking the stairs, they reached the hostel roof. All of them had brought dupattas and blankets with them. They sat on the roof and tied these together to make a rope-like structure. Then they tied it to the water tank pipe and started descending slowly. However, since the rope was too short, all five had to jump from a height of 15 feet. During this, the girl from Delhi injured her foot. The story after escaping from the shelter Called boyfriend from lounge, 1 boyfriend got scared The girls from Agra and Delhi told police that they managed to reach a lounge while trying to protect themselves. Here they made an excuse of injury. Then they called their boyfriends using someone's mobile phone. They informed them that they had escaped from the shelter home to meet them. 3 girls ran away home, caught from there The other 3 girls, who had fled from the shelter home on the pretext of helping, were also found at their respective homes. One girl's mother is not alive, and her father is in jail. When the father came out of jail on parole, he accused his sister's brother-in-law of eloping with the girl. After the girl was found, she was sent to the shelter home. The second girl had an affair with her aunt's son. In this case, the girl's mother and brother were opposing. However, her brother had also done a love marriage. In this case, when the girl was recovered, the mother said at the police station that they have nothing to do with her anymore, so she was sent to the shelter home. Girls seen in lobby CCTV, then disappeared On the morning of January 27, the shelter home staff discovered that 5 girls were missing. The home's superintendent Gayatri Mishra informed the administration officials and police. SSP Shlok Kumar arrived at the home. Police checked CCTV footage, the girls were visible in lobby cameras. However, there were no CCTV cameras installed at the spot from where they escaped. This caused initial difficulty in searching. Police kept searching for the girls in small hotels and lounges around the shelter home. A lounge revealed that 2 girls had come there that night. One had an injury on her foot. She had said that a car hit me. After this, she left from there at 8 am on Tuesday.

stories.title: Transgender skin therapist performs spiritual penance at Magh Mela:Says, 'Govt schemes for community are still not fully implemented'
stories.summary: Priyanshi Das, a transgender skin therapist from Prayagraj, shared her life story at the ongoing Magh Mela. “I was 7-8 years old when I realised my body didn’t match how I felt inside. I was born male, but my mind and identity were female. I loved dressing up and preparing myself like a girl,” she said. Priyanshi faced taunts from society and struggled to fit in during school and college. Despite attempts to discuss her feelings with her family, she found no support. “No one at home understood me, so I left and joined the transgender community,” she added. A large number of people come to her and take selfies. Dainik Bhaskar's team spoke to her in detail. Besides her, they also spoke to some other Kinnars. They understood the facilities and conveniences provided by the government. Let's find out what they shared… Joining the transgender community and pursuing education Priyanshi’s new community embraced her, and she completed her education. Today, she works as a cosmetologist and skin therapist, practicing in Odisha and Mumbai. She also became an activist, raising awareness about HIV/AIDS within the transgender community. “The transgender community faces discrimination in education and society. That’s why we started an organization to promote education and awareness. Initially, there were very few educated people in our society, and support was minimal. But persistence brought change,” she said. Spiritual practice at Magh Mela At the Magh Mela in Sector 6, where the transgender Akhara has a prominent presence, Priyanshi is currently performing spiritual practices and blessing devotees. Large crowds gather for blessings and selfies. She gives a coin and rice as a token of blessings. Supreme Court recognition and Government gaps The landmark 2014 Supreme Court ruling recognized transgender people as a third gender and directed the government to provide education and health services. “The decision gave us legal recognition, but many government schemes are not fully implemented. Reservation and job opportunities are still limited,” Priyanshi said. Mahamandaleshwar Kaushalya Giri of the Sanatan Transgender Akhara explained, “In Bihar, transgender people were given opportunities in police recruitment and home guard. But Uttar Pradesh has yet to implement similar provisions. We want even 1% reservation guaranteed; that’s enough to ensure stability for our community.” Challenges on the ground Mahamandaleshwar Sanjana Nand Giri, also from the Sanatan Akhara, emphasized the need for employment opportunities. “The younger generation needs education and jobs to avoid discrimination on the streets. Some states like Telangana, Chhattisgarh, and Jharkhand are implementing rules, including housing schemes. But much remains to be done,” she said.

stories.title: BJP's regional balance breaks down in UP:Gorakhpur and Kashi dominate Purvanchal, Awadh and western regions weaken
stories.summary: The regional balance in the UP BJP government and organisation has been disrupted. The dominance of the Kashi and Gorakhpur regions of Purvanchal has increased in key positions in both the government and the organisation, while Awadh and the western region remain the weakest. Political observers say that with the upcoming Assembly elections, the BJP will have to correct this imbalance, as its continuation could impact electoral outcomes. The BJP traditionally focuses on maintaining regional and social balance and often makes efforts to strike such equilibrium. However, this time both Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary hail from Gorakhpur district. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya is also from the Kashi region of Purvanchal. A large number of office-bearers in the party organisation are from Purvanchal as well. In contrast, Awadh and the western region have not been given comparable preference even within the organisation. CM Yogi is from Purvanchal. The Deputy CM is also from the Kashi region of Purvanchal, while Brajesh Pathak belongs to the Awadh region. Three office-bearers from a single district In the BJP’s state team, there are instances of three office-bearers coming from the same district. Several office-bearers have strategically changed their home district to Lucknow. State vice-presidents Trimbak Tripathi and Santosh Singh, along with general secretary Subhash Yaduvansh, are from Sant Kabir Nagar district. Similarly, vice-presidents Salil Vishnoi, Manvendra Singh, Kamalavati Singh and Devesh Kori are all from Kanpur district. Awadh and West lag behind in organisation too The BJP’s 45-member state team includes one state president, one general secretary (organisation), seven general secretaries, 18 vice-presidents and 16 ministers. Of these, five state vice-presidents, four of the seven general secretaries and five ministers are from Purvanchal. The western region does not have even a single state general secretary, though it has five vice-presidents and three state ministers. The Braj region has three state ministers, one general secretary and one vice-president. Awadh has four ministers and one general secretary, but not a single vice-president. Kanpur has one minister and four state vice-presidents, but no general secretary. New leadership fails to emerge Political analyst Virendra Nath Bhatt says that Purvanchal’s influence within the BJP is currently much higher, even though Awadh delivered the highest number of seats. He notes that when regional balance is not maintained, regions that lag behind in the organisation or government fail to produce new leadership. Shadow of UGC issue to remain Political analysts believe that although the Supreme Court has stayed the new UGC rules, the issue has not cooled down. Its impact will be visible in the formation of the BJP’s new team and the expansion of the cabinet in the coming period. Brahmins and Thakurs are likely to be given slightly more importance than before in the BJP team. In UP, the issue of Brahmin resentment is particularly prominent, and the BJP may give more opportunities to Brahmin faces to address it. Before 2014, Brahmins, Thakurs and Vaishyas had greater representation in the state team, but representation of the upper castes has steadily declined since then. Senior journalist Anand Rai says that the BJP suffered a major setback in Purvanchal, losing several seats there in the Lok Sabha elections. This is why more effort is now being focused on the region and its leaders are being promoted. He adds that despite being a large party, cabinet and state team positions are limited, making it impossible to provide leadership roles to all districts. Preparations to restore regional balance A BJP office-bearer said that organisational changes are expected in the coming days. A new team under state president Pankaj Chaudhary will be formed, and regional presidents of all six regions will also be changed. The party has realised that the regional balance has been disturbed. BJP leaders also acknowledge that this was one of the reasons behind the party’s defeat in 2024. As a result, in the upcoming organisational changes, the state and national leadership will attempt to restore regional balance to address the dissatisfaction among office-bearers.

Random Musing: Did 'The Matrix' foreshadow Jeffrey Epstein?

Uttarakhand opens 83 peaks in Garhwal and Kumaon regions for mountaineering
stories.summary: Uttarakhand has unlocked 83 Himalayan peaks, including Kamet and Nanda Devi East, for mountaineering, ranging from 5,700 to 7,756 meters. Indian climbers are now exempt from expedition fees, while foreign climbers benefit from reduced state charges. A new online portal streamlines applications, boosting tourism and local employment in remote areas.

stories.title: US-Iran tensions: Tehran signals readiness for talks amid Trump's pressure
stories.summary: Iran's President Pezeshkian has ordered talks with the US, seeking an environment free from threats and unreasonable expectations, focusing on national interests. This comes amid heightened regional tensions and a warning from President Trump about potential "bad things." Tehran insists negotiations must center on the nuclear issue, not defense capabilities.

1200 years after it was destroyed, a new Nalanda is taking shape
Delhi horror: 36-year-old businessman dies days after being hit with helmet by delivery agents
stories.summary: A 36-year-old businessman, Shivam Gupta, tragically passed away after a brutal assault by food delivery agents in Delhi. The incident, stemming from a verbal dispute over water, escalated into a violent attack involving punches, kicks, and a helmet. Shivam's family is devastated, demanding swift justice for the senseless loss of their only child.

stories.title: 'Considering impeachment motion': TMC plans big move against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over West Bengal SIR
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee announced plans to move an impeachment motion against the Chief Election Commissioner over the Special Intensive Revision process. The party alleges the SIR is flawed and aims to disenfranchise citizens, particularly in opposition-ruled states ahead of elections. West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee also criticized the timing and selective application of the SIR.

stories.title: 75-country Green Card freeze: US announces adoption waiver in new update

stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party's Yumnam Khemchand has been elected as the leader of the legislative party and is set to become the new chief minister of Manipur. This development follows a meeting of BJP legislative members in Delhi. Khemchand, a senior leader, previously served as the assembly speaker and a cabinet minister.

stories.title: 'Blot on our democracy': Rahul Gandhi writes to Speaker Om Birla; says 'deliberate attempt' to stop him from speaking in House
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has lodged a strong protest with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, citing his inability to speak on the President's address. Gandhi claims he was prevented from quoting an unpublished book by former Army Chief General MM Naravane on the India-China clashes, calling it a "blot on our democracy" and a deliberate government attempt to silence him.

stories.title: 'Punjabi Devils' bike gang founder Jashanpreet pleads guilty in US in illegal possession of arms case
Qatar-based expat wins big ticket, plans heartwarming prize for his daughter
stories.summary: A Qatar-based expat, Vinoth Anbarasan, won Dh50,000 in the Big Ticket raffle. He plans to share the winnings with friends and create a special memory for his daughter. The Big Ticket draw has been a popular event for over 30 years, offering hope and significant prizes to expatriates across the Gulf.

stories.title: 3 Indians arrested in Surrey for extortion shooting after Canada city mayor's call for 'emergency'
Journal retracts study comparing homoeopathy and standard care in infants
stories.summary: A significant study comparing homoeopathy with conventional infant care has been retracted by the European Journal of Pediatrics due to serious design flaws, including a lack of blinding and placebo controls. These issues, the journal stated, could have introduced substantial bias, undermining the study's reliability. The authors, however, disagree with the retraction.

stories.title: Fuel switch scare: Air India to send 'impacted' component for checks - what DGCA said
'Take immediate action’: MEA condemns theft of Mahatma Gandhi statue in Australia
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs has strongly condemned the theft of Mahatma Gandhi's bronze statue from the Australian Indian Community Centre in Melbourne. The ministry has urged Australian authorities to take immediate action to recover the statue and hold the perpetrators accountable for the act.

stories.title: Green Card holders won't get SBA loans in US from March 1: What this new rule means for Indians
Evening news wrap: PM Modi hails India-US trade deal at NDA meet; Russia fires over 70 missiles, 450 drones at Ukraine; & more
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi hailed the India-US trade deal as a significant national benefit, while Rahul Gandhi alleged it was signed under pressure. Meanwhile, Russia intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy grid, causing widespread heating outages. In India, eight opposition MPs faced suspension from Lok Sabha for disruptive behavior. Pakistan's defence minister highlighted challenges in Balochistan amidst rising militant violence.

stories.title: MrBeast mocks Elon Musk’s SpaceX and xAI merger announcement with a cheeky tweet that sends X into a frenzy
stories.summary: MrBeast sparked online buzz after joking about Elon Musk’s announcement that SpaceX and xAI have merged into one company. Responding to Musk’s celebratory post, the YouTuber quipped about posting on a SpaceX-owned platform, sending X into a frenzy. The lighthearted jab drew widespread reactions and briefly stole attention from the $1.25 trillion merger itself.

stories.title: Dubai authorities reveal two key locations for the futuristic Dubai Loop
stories.summary: Dubai is launching its revolutionary underground transport system, the Dubai Loop, in partnership with Elon Musk's The Boring Company. This high-speed network aims to bypass traffic congestion, starting with a crucial link between DIFC and Dubai Mall. The project promises faster, integrated travel, with initial test runs anticipated by 2026, transforming urban mobility.

stories.title: 'They called me yaar, tore and threw papers': TDP's Krishna Tenneti slams eight suspended Lok Sabha MPs
'Hard to understand': Indian CEO says his US visa for an investor meeting got rejected for no reason
Union Budget 2026-27 shakes up NRI money: What Indians in UAE must do now
stories.summary: India's Union Budget 2026-27 brings welcome changes for NRIs in the UAE. Investment limits in Indian equities have doubled, making it easier to build stakes. Property sales compliance is simplified, reducing administrative hurdles. Overseas travel and education remittances see reduced taxes, lowering costs. These reforms aim to boost diaspora engagement with India's economy.

stories.title: Musk’s X faces probe in France as prosecutors search office over child-abuse content, deepfakes
stories.summary: French prosecutors are conducting searches at X's Paris offices as part of an investigation into alleged child abuse material, deepfakes, and data manipulation. Elon Musk and CEO Linda Yaccarino have been asked for voluntary interviews. The probe, initiated by a lawmaker's concerns about algorithms, has expanded to include issues with the AI chatbot Grok.

stories.title: Punjab 'completely ignored' in Union budget yet again: Finance Minister Cheema
“She was going to marry Charlie”: Laura Loomer reignites speculation about Candace Owens and Charlie Kirk’s relationship
stories.summary: Laura Loomer sparked fresh controversy after claiming Candace Owens believed she would one day marry the late Charlie Kirk. The accusation followed Owens’ renewed public comments about Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk. Loomer’s post revived long standing speculation about Owens’ motives, blurring the line between political disagreement, personal grief, and unresolved tensions within conservative media circles.

stories.title: Bihar, Assam, Chhattisgarh lead the way in installing smart electricity meters: Govt in Rajya Sabha
IndiGo issues travel advisory amid Iran conflict: Flights to and from Tbilisi, Almaty, Baku, and Tashkent cancelled till February 28
stories.summary: Amidst escalating Iran tensions, IndiGo has extended flight cancellations to Tbilisi, Almaty, Baku, and Tashkent until February 28, 2026. The airline is rerouting to ensure passenger and crew safety, as its usual flight paths traverse Iranian airspace. This move comes as US-Iran relations remain volatile, though diplomatic efforts are reportedly underway.

stories.title: USA expands visa curbs to 39 countries - should UAE residents worry?
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of State has expanded visa restrictions for citizens of 39 countries deemed "non-compliant." This policy, under Section 243(d) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, impacts visitor, student, and immigrant visas. While UAE nationals are unaffected, expats from these nations residing in the UAE will face stricter rules and potential delays for U.S. travel.

stories.title: 'A big decision that would benefit everyone': PM Modi on India-US trade deal at NDA meet
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi hailed the India-US trade deal as a significant decision benefiting all citizens. The agreement, announced by President Trump, will see the US reduce tariffs on Indian goods to 18% from 50%. India is expected to eliminate its tariffs and non-tariff barriers on US products, potentially boosting trade significantly.

stories.title: Inside China’s gray zone activities: How Beijing is salami slicing its way to influence
stories.summary: China is employing a 'salami slicing' strategy, taking incremental steps across military, economic, and technological domains to alter realities without triggering conflict. This 'gray zone' approach, evident in the South China Sea and beyond, bypasses international law and exploits rivals' hesitation. The cumulative effect creates new facts on the ground, challenging the existing order.

stories.title: 'PM under pressure': Rahul Gandhi links Adani, Epstein to India-US trade deal
'Our Prime Minister compromised, sold our nation': Rahul Gandhi outside Parliament after LS snub

stories.title: Dubai unveils driverless pod routes connecting metro stations to major destinations
stories.summary: Dubai is set to revolutionize urban transit with Glydways, an autonomous electric pod system launching within four months. These driverless vehicles will operate on dedicated tracks, tackling the "last-mile" challenge and aiming to eliminate traffic congestion. This initiative is a significant step towards Dubai's goal of 25% autonomous trips by 2030.

stories.title: BTS in Dubai? K-pop fans can't keep calm as OT7 spotted flying to the UAE
stories.summary: Global K-pop sensation BTS has been spotted leaving for Dubai. The pap videos from the airport have excited fans worldwide. It marks a significant reunion for the group after their military service. Speculation is rife about their upcoming album 'Arirang' and a massive world tour. The visit also hints at potential future entertainment collaborations in the UAE.

stories.summary: The UAE Fatwa Council has declared the traditional Haq Al Laila celebration permissible under Islamic law, provided it aligns with core principles. This mid-Sha'ban festivity, involving children collecting sweets and community gatherings, strengthens family and social bonds. The ruling permits cultural observances and spiritual reflection, encouraging unity and joy as Ramadan nears.

The article provides a detailed daily timetable for Suhoor, Iftar, and Isha prayers, aiding in planning for this sacred period.

Gaiman vehemently denies these claims, calling them untrue and a smear campaign. The situation has ignited widespread debate about consent, evidence, media coverage, and the separation of art from the artist.

stories.title: UAE announces prayer timings for today: Fajr at 5:37am, Maghrib at sunset
stories.summary: Official prayer timings for Tuesday, February 3, 2026, have been released by AWQAF across the UAE, with Fajr prayers commencing at 5:41 AM in Abu Dhabi and 5:37 AM in Dubai. The article also highlights post-prayer practices like Dhikr and Ayat al-Kursi recitation for spiritual clarity. Ramadan 2026 is anticipated to begin around February 18th, falling during the cooler season.

stories.title: One million AI satellites to orbit Earth? SpaceX's mind-blowing plan of data centers in outer space explained
stories.summary: SpaceX has proposed a radical plan to deploy up to a million solar-powered satellites as orbital data centers for AI. This ambitious project aims to meet soaring AI compute demands, offering potential energy efficiency over terrestrial facilities. While promising a revolution in computing, the proposal faces significant concerns regarding space debris, regulation and technical feasibility.

Concerns were raised over India reportedly agreeing to zero tariffs on US goods and potentially halting Russian oil purchases.

stories.title: Dubai RTA’s premium number plate auction is back: 300 chances to own a coveted plate
stories.summary: Dubai's RTA is hosting its 82nd online auction for 300 premium vehicle number plates starting February 9, 2026. Residents can bid on unique 2- to 5-digit combinations, reflecting the city's car culture and personal expression. Registration has opened. These plates are highly sought after, often fetching millions, symbolising status and potential investment.

stories.title: Ram Rahim plea: HC resumes hearing in journo murder case

Counsel for Gurmeet Ram Rahim contended that he was not named in the first chargesheet filed by police in 2002 and that his name was included in it “by way of revenge”.

stories.summary: Asked about Parth, Pune commissioner of police (CP) Amitesh Kumar said on Monday: “Our investigation so far has not revealed any involvement.” Although Parth has not been named in the FIR, Digvijay Amarsinh Patil, another of Amadea’s partners, and arrested tehsildar Suryakant Yewale are mentioned. Tejwani and Patil were signatories to the deal last year.

CPM workers were convicted and handed double life terms by a trial court. Tenth accused Ranjith T was granted 15-day parole Monday, barely two-and-a-half months after similar relief earlier.

stories.title: 3,000 illegal birth & death certificates cancelled in Maharashtra
stories.summary: The district administration conducted a thorough investigation and found that there was no record of these names. The health department raised the issue with state govt and informed the state registrar. Following directives from the state registrar, the health department started cancelling the certificates. So far, close to 3,000 certificates have been cancelled. The entire process will be completed in a week’s time.

stories.title: NCP vs NCP(SP): Bhujbal, Mushrif deny merger talks were on

Those speaking of a merger should answer whether they are fine with it.”

That creates immense pressure on pilots to land at the intended destination at all costs, even when diversion would be the safer option,” said Capt Manoj Hathi, former senior flight operations inspector at the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).

stories.summary: The findings are based on an analysis of more than a century of lifespan data from large Scandinavian twin cohorts in Denmark and Sweden. Researchers studied identical and non-identical twins raised together and apart, as well as siblings of US centenarians. Most participants were born between 1870 and 1935, a period marked by high mortality from infectious diseases and accidents.

stories.title: Abhimanyu experiment: MP govt hosps to get Garbh Sanskar rooms to ‘educate mind of fetus’
stories.summary: These dedicated spaces are meant to guide expectant parents through prenatal care rooted in traditional Indian practices, from positive thinking and lifestyle discipline to diet and emotional well-being. The idea: shape the mind of the unborn. CM Mohan Yadav announced the initiative Sunday in Indore, placing it under the Ayushman Bharat scheme and linking it to the Union ministry of Ayush.

stories.title: Piers Morgan reacts strongly as Candace Owens podcast sparks outrage over Erika Kirk jokes and Charlie Kirk theories
stories.summary: Piers Morgan condemned Candace Owens and Bassem Youssef after comments about Erika Kirk sparked backlash online. The remarks followed a podcast discussion that questioned her behavior during a leaked Zoom call. Morgan called the jokes cruel and unsupported by facts. He continues to challenge Owens to prove her claims or publicly retract them.

stories.title: Billie Eilish roasted after 'stolen land' remarks at Grammys: 'Return your $14 million LA mansion'
At 90, Dalai Lama gets Grammy for audiobook ‘Meditations’
stories.summary: The Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), which is headquartered at McLeod Ganj in Dharamshala, said the award is a profound honour for Tibetan society. Although the Grammy spread cheer in this hill town, celebrations are on hold as the Dalai Lama is in Karnataka. American singer-songwriter Rufus Wainwright received the award on his behalf.

stories.title: For caste census, mere self-declaration cannot be enough: SC
stories.summary: Appearing for social activist Akash Goel, advocate Mukta Gupta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that the directorate of census operations, which has commenced preparatory work for Census 2027, has not disclosed “any predetermined criteria or standardised methodology” for recording caste identity of people belonging to SC, ST and OBC categories during census.

stories.title: Parents to be blamed for allowing minors to drink & drive: SC
stories.summary: A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan said that there cannot be punishment before trial and directed release of the accused who already spent 18 months in jail. They were allegedly involved in tampering of evidence by swapping blood samples of their kids with their own. Father of the main accused, who is a minor and was allegedly driving the case, is still in jail.

stories.title: Rottweiler attack leaves Bengaluru woman with over 80 stitches
stories.summary: Days that once revolved around work, cuddles and caring for her breastfeeding child are now spent in a hospital bed, recovering from a brutal dog attack that has left her with more than 80 stitches across her face, throat and head — and scars that go far beyond the physical. Early on Jan 26, Shalini had stepped out for morning walk near home in HSR Layout’s Teachers’ Colony.

stories.title: Wangchuk tried to create Nepal and Bangladesh-like unrest: Govt tells SC
stories.summary: Appearing before a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and P B Varale, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said the activist was appealing to Gen Z to come out on the street against govt to create a problem in Ladakh which is very sensitive as it shares borders with countries that are not very friendly. Responding to Wangchuk’s submission that he was holding a peaceful protest against govt on the line of Gandhian principles, the SG said, “Gandhi was just a facade to hide his real intention of instigating violence.”

stories.title: Stanford students pretend to be Jains to escape $7,944 mandatory meal plan
stories.summary: A Stanford student's essay alleging undergraduates falsely claim Jain identity to bypass mandatory meal plans has sparked debate. The claim, based on anecdotal evidence, suggests students exploit religious exemptions to redirect dining funds. This controversy highlights broader student frustration with expensive, inflexible campus dining and the challenges universities face in balancing accommodations with potential misuse.

stories.title: SC notice to govt as church body challenges anti-conversion laws
stories.summary: One of the laws challenged by the association is the nearly 60-year-old Orissa Freedom of Religion Act, 1967. Madhya Pradesh had enacted Chhattisgarh Dharma Swatantrya Adhiniyam in 1968 to prevent large-scale conversion of tribals. SC had upheld the constitutional validity of the Orissa and MP laws in 1977 in Rev Stanislaus vs State of MP case and said while the right to propagate religion is a fundamental right, it does not include right to convert.

stories.title: Manipur set for govt, BJP MLAs to elect leader; Biren to be replaced
stories.summary: Official sources said BJP MLAs are in the national capital and will be electing a new leader, who will be sworn in as the new chief minister. The party has not officially declared a date for the legislative party meeting and named its general secretary Tarun Chugh as the central observer for the election of the new leader.

stories.title: TMC vs EC: Poll body red flags abusive language by Trinamool MLAs
stories.summary: While also listing blatant violations of EC’s lawful directions by the Bengal administration, CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Monday firmly conveyed to Mamata that the “rule of law shall prevail and anybody taking law into their own hands shall be dealt with strictly, as per provisions of law and powers vested in the Commission”. “No pressure, obstruction, or interference of any kind by anyone should be exerted on officers engaged in SIR work,” it was underlined.

stories.title: Bengal SIR row: Didi storms out of meet with CEC, claims being ‘humiliated’
stories.summary: Talking to reporters later in front of Nirvachan Sadan — where a heavy police posse had gathered — she claimed to have warned the CEC that he will end up like Jagdeep Dhankhar, seen as a reference to the former VP’s sudden resignation last year. She was accompanied by party national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, MP Kalyan Banerjee, and 12 members from what they claimed were “SIR-affected families” from Bengal.

stories.title: 12-yr-old lured into trading Rs 85L jewellery for ‘unlimited momos’
stories.summary: According to a complaint filed by the boy’s father, a temple priest, the child had grown fond of momo sold at the roadside stall. The vendors allegedly began feeding him free of cost, winning trust bite by bite. Soon came bigger offers — food, small sums of money, loyalty. Then persuasion. Unaware of the stakes, the boy began removing jewellery from home and handing it over, police said.

stories.title: Jeffrey Epstein has a ‘secret son’? Explosive DOJ emails show he was congratulated for ‘baby boy’
stories.summary: Newly released DOJ documents reveal an email from Sarah Ferguson seemingly congratulating Jeffrey Epstein on a “baby boy,” suggesting he may have had a secret child, though this remains unverified. The files also show Ferguson’s frustration over Epst'ein using her to access Prince Andrew, reveal Andrew’s continued contact with Epstein until 2017, and highlight Epstein’s extensive high-level connections. Allegations remain unproven.

stories.title: Gen Naravane's memoir: Rules bar retired officers from publishing classified info
stories.summary: Senior military officials, particularly those dealing with classified information, are subject to regulations under the Official Secrets Act that restrict the publication of books or information even after retirement to prevent such classified material from becoming public. While a general one-year “cooling-off” period exists for taking up commercial or private employment, regulations for publishing secret content require prior govt clearance.

stories.title: Rahul quotes from ex-Gen’s unpublished book on China row, gets Shah, Rajnath rap
stories.summary: Speaker Om Birla failed to defuse the situation even after he gave a ruling asking Gandhi not to refer to news articles or extracts from an unpublished book and speak only on what could be authenticated by placing it on record. The LoP maintained that he should be allowed to speak on the issue, saying excerpts of the unpublished book had been published in Caravan magazine and were authentic.

stories.title: ‘No mechanical arrests over social media posts’: SC upholds HC order
stories.summary: The SC order may end the prevalent practice harassing people by filing mulitple cases against those whose social media post is critical of govt or party in power, and safeguards fundamental rights. The guidelines say the police must verify whether the complainant qualifies as the “person aggrieved” in terms of law before registering a case and conduct a preliminary probe before lodging an FIR.

stories.title: Minneapolis school where ICE detained 5-year-old receives bomb threat
Amid threats to ‘chicken’s neck’, India to take rail corridor underground
stories.summary: Ashwini Vaishnaw said the Budget contains a proposal to expand railway link between the region and the rest of the country to four tracks, fulfilling a long-felt need. Northeast Frontier Railway GM Chetan Shrivastava said the underground stretch would run from Tin Mile Haat to Rangapani stations within Bengal. During the 2017 Doklam stand-off, military planners had talked about the vulnerability of the Siliguri stretch of the corridor.

stories.title: Khaby Lame net worth: Inside the $1 billion Rich Sparkle Holdings deal that raised billionaire rumors around TikTok star
stories.summary: Khaby Lame’s nearly $1 billion deal is an all-stock agreement with Rich Sparkle Holdings, not a cash payout. The deal makes him a major shareholder and includes plans for an AI digital version of him. Despite online rumors, he has not retired and did not receive upfront cash.

stories.title: AI Boeing fuel switch cuts off again, this time at UK airport
stories.summary: The switch moved without the required lift action, suggesting the safeguard meant to prevent fuel supply cut off and inadvertent engine shutdown did not function as designed, sources said. The London incident challenges the controversial narrative that the Ahmedabad crash resulted from a deliberate pilot act, pointing instead to a possible and critical technical flaw in the aircraft’s fuel switch design.

stories.title: Nick Fuentes shocked as Kick ends partnership just days after approval
stories.summary: Online streamer Nicholas J. Fuentes saw his Kick partnership abruptly revoked just days after approval, sparking concerns over the platform's opaque policies. Despite boasting significant viewership, Fuentes received no explanation for the sudden termination. This incident highlights a pattern of inconsistent decisions on emerging platforms, leaving creators questioning transparency and fairness.

stories.title: Who is Nancy Guthrie? 84-year-old mother of NBC’s ‘Today’ show host Savannah Guthrie reported missing
Hasan Piker back on Twitch as platform shortens suspension to three days
stories.summary: Hasan Piker, also known as HasanAbi, has returned to Twitch after a three-day suspension, reduced from seven days following an appeal. While Twitch hasn't officially confirmed the reason, reports suggest it stemmed from his use of the phrase "Zionist-pigs." During his ban, Piker continued streaming on YouTube, attracting significant viewership and donations for immigration advocacy groups.

stories.title: Norway Crown Princess says she regrets connection with Epstein whom she called 'sweetheart' in email: I showed poor judgement
Move beyond law varsity demand, press for J&K’s statehood, Omar’s NC tells BJP
stories.summary: J&K has no NLU at present but the demand for it to be located in Jammu gained traction after CM Omar said last year that it would come up in Kashmir’s Budgam. Omar has rejected the recent BJP demands, calling the controversy “politically motivated” and pointing out that there were no protests in the Valley when Jammu was given both an IIT and an IIM.

stories.title: Two suspects detained in Samba; searches launched in Udhampur
stories.summary: On Jan 6, Punjab Police detained a minor in Pathankot on charges of spying and for allegedly sharing confidential information via social media to terror agencies, ISI, and Pakistan military officers. The detention prompted a statewide alert for similar espionage activities involving children. Under Operation Trashi-I, security forces have engaged in four encounters with terrorists in the past fortnight.

stories.title: ‘Hired green card, US citizen drivers’: Sikh truck company owner after losing employees as California revoked thousands of licences
Man raised as a girl learns at 19 he was born intersex and surgically altered as a baby by his parents
stories.summary: Jim Ambrose was raised as a girl after doctors surgically altered his intersex body at birth without his consent. Discovering the truth at 19 reframed his entire life, exposing medical harm, secrecy, and lost autonomy. His story explores identity, anger, healing, and the lasting impact of irreversible decisions made for children.
